title: AWS Certified Advanced Networking – Specialty (ANS-C01) practice questions

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design a solution that incorporates edge network services to optimize user performance and traffic management for global architectures
questions.question: A global e-commerce site serves dynamic API responses and static assets from us-east-1. Users in Asia report slow page loads. Which design improves performance for both content types?
options: Put Amazon CloudFront in front of the origin, caching static assets and using CloudFront for dynamic requests to benefit from the AWS backbone and persistent origin connections
Increase the size of the origin instances
Use Route 53 simple routing with a long TTL
Move only the static assets to an S3 bucket in us-east-1
questions.correct_rationale: CloudFront caches static content near users and accelerates dynamic requests over optimized connections.
questions.distractor_summary: Bigger origins do not reduce distance, DNS TTL does not speed delivery, and an S3 bucket in the same Region stays far from Asian users.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design a solution that incorporates edge network services to optimize user performance and traffic management for global architectures
questions.question: A gaming company uses UDP for real-time play and needs static IP addresses that clients can allowlist, with traffic routed to the nearest healthy Regional endpoint. Which service fits best?
options: Amazon CloudFront with a custom origin
Route 53 geolocation routing to Elastic IPs
An Application Load Balancer in each Region with no global layer
AWS Global Accelerator with endpoint groups in each Region
questions.correct_rationale: Global Accelerator provides two static anycast IPs, supports UDP, and routes over the AWS backbone to healthy endpoints.
questions.distractor_summary: CloudFront handles HTTP and WebSocket rather than arbitrary UDP, DNS-based routing depends on resolver caching, and Regional ALBs need a global entry point.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design a solution that incorporates edge network services to optimize user performance and traffic management for global architectures
questions.question: Which Global Accelerator feature lets you direct a percentage of traffic to a specific Region, for example during a blue/green migration?
options: Client affinity
Health check grace periods
Traffic dials on endpoint groups
Custom routing accelerators
questions.correct_rationale: Traffic dials control the percentage of traffic sent to each endpoint group.
questions.distractor_summary: Client affinity keeps users on the same endpoint, health check settings affect failover, and custom routing maps users to specific destinations.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design a solution that incorporates edge network services to optimize user performance and traffic management for global architectures
questions.question: A media company wants to run lightweight code at CloudFront edge locations to rewrite URLs and add security headers with sub-millisecond latency. Which feature fits best?
options: Lambda@Edge on origin request only
CloudFront Functions on viewer request and viewer response events
An EC2 instance in every Region
Route 53 traffic policies
questions.correct_rationale: CloudFront Functions are designed for lightweight, high-scale header and URL manipulation at the edge.
questions.distractor_summary: Lambda@Edge suits heavier logic and network calls, EC2 fleets add operations, and Route 53 policies do not modify requests.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design a solution that incorporates edge network services to optimize user performance and traffic management for global architectures
questions.question: A company must serve private video content only to paying subscribers through CloudFront for a limited time. What should be implemented?
options: A public S3 bucket with obscure object names
CloudFront signed URLs or signed cookies with an expiration, and origin access control on the S3 origin
Security groups on the CloudFront distribution
Geo restriction for all countries except one
questions.correct_rationale: Signed URLs or cookies grant time-limited access, and OAC prevents direct origin access.
questions.distractor_summary: Obscure names are not protection, CloudFront does not use security groups, and geo restriction does not verify subscribers.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design a solution that incorporates edge network services to optimize user performance and traffic management for global architectures
questions.question: What is the purpose of CloudFront Origin Shield?
options: An additional caching layer that reduces load on the origin by consolidating requests from edge locations
A DDoS protection product
A WAF rule group
An origin encryption setting
questions.correct_rationale: Origin Shield adds a central cache to improve hit ratio and protect the origin.
questions.distractor_summary: DDoS protection is Shield, WAF rules filter requests, and encryption is configured separately.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design a solution that incorporates edge network services to optimize user performance and traffic management for global architectures
questions.question: Users in a specific country must reach a localized version of a website, and the decision should happen at DNS resolution. Which Route 53 routing policy fits best?
options: Latency-based routing
Weighted routing
Multivalue answer routing
Geolocation routing
questions.correct_rationale: Geolocation routing answers based on the user's location.
questions.distractor_summary: Latency routing chooses the fastest Region, weighted splits by percentage, and multivalue returns several records.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design a solution that incorporates edge network services to optimize user performance and traffic management for global architectures
questions.question: A company wants to shift traffic gradually toward users' nearest Region but also bias more users toward a newly expanded Region. Which Route 53 policy allows this?
options: Simple routing
Failover routing
Geoproximity routing with a positive bias for the new Region (using Route 53 traffic flow)
Multivalue answer routing
questions.correct_rationale: Geoproximity routing considers location and lets you expand or shrink a Region's area with bias.
questions.distractor_summary: Simple and multivalue routing do not use location bias, and failover routes only to a secondary when the primary fails.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design a solution that incorporates edge network services to optimize user performance and traffic management for global architectures
questions.question: Which CloudFront feature compresses responses automatically to reduce transfer size?
options: Field-level encryption
Signed cookies
Automatic compression with gzip or Brotli in the cache behavior
Real-time logs
questions.correct_rationale: CloudFront can compress eligible responses when viewers accept compression.
questions.distractor_summary: Field-level encryption protects data, signed cookies control access, and logs record requests.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design a solution that incorporates edge network services to optimize user performance and traffic management for global architectures
questions.question: A public API behind CloudFront must protect against common web attacks at the edge. What should be attached?
options: A network ACL on the origin subnet only
An AWS WAF web ACL on the CloudFront distribution
An S3 bucket policy
A VPC endpoint policy
questions.correct_rationale: WAF filters malicious HTTP requests at edge locations before they reach the origin.
questions.distractor_summary: Network ACLs cannot inspect HTTP, bucket policies apply to S3, and endpoint policies apply to VPC endpoints.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design a solution that incorporates edge network services to optimize user performance and traffic management for global architectures
questions.question: A company's ALB origin is in a private subnet and must be reachable only through CloudFront, without exposing a public load balancer. Which feature fits best?
options: CloudFront VPC origins pointing to the internal ALB
A public ALB with an open security group
A NAT gateway in front of the ALB
Route 53 private hosted zone records for viewers
questions.correct_rationale: VPC origins let CloudFront deliver content from private ALBs, NLBs, or EC2 instances.
questions.distractor_summary: Public open ALBs expose the origin, NAT gateways handle outbound traffic, and private zones are not visible to internet viewers.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design a solution that incorporates edge network services to optimize user performance and traffic management for global architectures
questions.question: Which header can CloudFront add to requests so the origin can verify they came from the distribution?
options: The Host header set to the viewer's IP
The X-Forwarded-For header only
The Content-Length header
A custom origin header with a secret value
questions.correct_rationale: A secret custom header checked by the origin or WAF confirms requests came through CloudFront.
questions.distractor_summary: The other headers do not prove the request path.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design a solution that incorporates edge network services to optimize user performance and traffic management for global architectures
questions.question: A company uses AWS Global Accelerator in front of NLBs in two Regions. Users must stay connected to the same endpoint for stateful sessions. What should be configured?
options: Traffic dial set to 0 percent
A longer health check interval
Weighted routing in Route 53
Client affinity set to source IP
questions.correct_rationale: Source IP client affinity keeps a client's traffic going to the same endpoint.
questions.distractor_summary: Traffic dials adjust volume, health check intervals affect detection, and Route 53 is not used for Global Accelerator affinity.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design a solution that incorporates edge network services to optimize user performance and traffic management for global architectures
questions.question: Video segments are cached poorly because query strings with tracking IDs make every URL unique. How can the cache hit ratio improve?
options: Turn off caching
Lower the TTL to zero
Use a cache policy that excludes irrelevant query strings, headers, and cookies from the cache key
Add more origins
questions.correct_rationale: Removing unneeded values from the cache key lets requests share cached objects.
questions.distractor_summary: Disabling caching or zero TTLs make it worse, and more origins do not fix cache keys.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Design a solution that incorporates edge network services to optimize user performance and traffic management for global architectures
questions.question: What is the main benefit of anycast IP addresses used by Global Accelerator?
options: They encrypt all traffic automatically
Users connect to the nearest AWS edge location advertising the same IP, entering the AWS network quickly
They remove the need for health checks
They provide private connectivity to VPCs from on premises
questions.correct_rationale: Anycast routes users to the closest edge location announcing the IP.
questions.distractor_summary: Anycast does not encrypt, replace health checks, or provide private hybrid connectivity.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design DNS solutions that meet public, private, and hybrid requirements
questions.question: Workloads in several VPCs must resolve internal names in a private domain. Which Route 53 feature fits best?
options: A private hosted zone associated with each VPC
A public hosted zone with private IP records
Hosts files on every instance
A DNS server in a single VPC with no forwarding
questions.correct_rationale: Private hosted zones answer queries only from associated VPCs.
questions.distractor_summary: Public zones expose internal names, hosts files do not scale, and an isolated DNS server is not reachable by others.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design DNS solutions that meet public, private, and hybrid requirements
questions.question: A private hosted zone in account A must be associated with a VPC in account B. What is the process?
options: Create an association authorization in account A, then associate the VPC from account B
Share the zone through a public URL
Copy all records into a new zone in account B
It cannot be done across accounts
questions.correct_rationale: Cross-account association requires authorization from the zone owner and association from the VPC owner.
questions.distractor_summary: Zones are not shared through URLs, copying records drifts, and cross-account association is supported.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design DNS solutions that meet public, private, and hybrid requirements
questions.question: Which Route 53 Resolver component forwards DNS queries from a VPC to on-premises DNS servers?
options: An inbound endpoint
A public hosted zone
A health check
An outbound endpoint with forwarding rules
questions.correct_rationale: Outbound endpoints send queries that match forwarding rules to target DNS servers.
questions.distractor_summary: Inbound endpoints receive queries from on premises, public zones host internet records, and health checks monitor endpoints.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design DNS solutions that meet public, private, and hybrid requirements
questions.question: On-premises servers must resolve names in Route 53 private hosted zones. What should be configured?
options: An outbound endpoint only
A public hosted zone copy
A Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint and conditional forwarders on the on-premises DNS servers pointing to its IP addresses
VPC DNS hostnames disabled
questions.correct_rationale: Inbound endpoints give on-premises resolvers targets inside the VPC.
questions.distractor_summary: Outbound endpoints serve the opposite direction, public copies expose records, and disabling hostnames does not help.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design DNS solutions that meet public, private, and hybrid requirements
questions.question: A company has 100 VPCs across many accounts that must use the same forwarding rules to on-premises DNS. How can this be managed centrally?
options: Create rules separately in every account
Create Resolver rules in a central networking account and share them with AWS RAM, associating them with VPCs in other accounts
Use one VPC for all workloads
Use hosts files
questions.correct_rationale: Shared Resolver rules let many VPCs use a central outbound endpoint.
questions.distractor_summary: Per-account rules are hard to maintain, a single VPC removes isolation, and hosts files do not scale.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design DNS solutions that meet public, private, and hybrid requirements
questions.question: What is a Route 53 alias record?
options: A CNAME that costs extra per query to AWS resources
A Route 53-specific record that points to AWS resources such as ALBs or CloudFront and can be used at the zone apex
A TXT record for verification
A private hosted zone
questions.correct_rationale: Alias records route to AWS resources and work at the apex, unlike CNAMEs.
questions.distractor_summary: Alias queries to AWS resources are free, and they are not TXT records or zones.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design DNS solutions that meet public, private, and hybrid requirements
questions.question: A company wants DNS query logs for all queries made by resources in its VPCs to detect suspicious lookups. What should be enabled?
options: Route 53 Resolver query logging to CloudWatch Logs, S3, or Firehose
Route 53 public hosted zone query logging only
VPC Flow Logs
CloudTrail data events
questions.correct_rationale: Resolver query logging captures queries originating from VPCs.
questions.distractor_summary: Public zone logging covers internet queries to your zone, Flow Logs lack query names, and CloudTrail records API calls.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design DNS solutions that meet public, private, and hybrid requirements
questions.question: DNSSEC must be enabled for a public domain hosted in Route 53. What is required?
options: Enable DNSSEC only on the registrar without signing the zone
Turn on Resolver query logging
Use a private hosted zone
Enable DNSSEC signing for the hosted zone with a KMS key-signing key and add the DS record at the parent zone or registrar
questions.correct_rationale: Zone signing plus a DS record at the parent establishes the chain of trust.
questions.distractor_summary: Registrar settings alone do not sign records, logging is unrelated, and private zones are not public DNSSEC.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design DNS solutions that meet public, private, and hybrid requirements
questions.question: Which VPC attributes must be enabled for private hosted zones to work?
options: enableNetworkAddressUsageMetrics only
An internet gateway attachment
enableDnsSupport and enableDnsHostnames
A NAT gateway
questions.correct_rationale: DNS support and DNS hostnames must be enabled for private hosted zone resolution.
questions.distractor_summary: Usage metrics, internet gateways, and NAT gateways are not required.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design DNS solutions that meet public, private, and hybrid requirements
questions.question: Overlapping domain names exist: a private hosted zone and an on-premises zone both host corp.example.com. Queries for some on-premises records fail from AWS. What explains this?
options: DNS always queries on premises first
Private hosted zones are ignored in VPCs
Route 53 Resolver answers from the private hosted zone for that domain and does not fall back to on premises for missing records, unless a more specific forwarding rule exists
Forwarding rules cannot use subdomains
questions.correct_rationale: When a private zone matches, Resolver returns its answer and does not forward missing names; more specific rules can override.
questions.distractor_summary: The other statements describe resolution incorrectly.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design DNS solutions that meet public, private, and hybrid requirements
questions.question: A hybrid environment needs a central DNS architecture that avoids running DNS servers on EC2. Which design fits best?
options: A pair of BIND servers on EC2 in each VPC
Route 53 Resolver inbound and outbound endpoints in a shared services VPC, with shared rules and private hosted zones associated across VPCs
Public hosted zones for internal names
Hosts files synchronized nightly
questions.correct_rationale: Resolver endpoints provide managed hybrid DNS without self-managed servers.
questions.distractor_summary: BIND fleets add operations, public zones expose names, and hosts files do not scale.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Design DNS solutions that meet public, private, and hybrid requirements
questions.question: Which Route 53 health check type monitors the status of other health checks?
options: Calculated health checks
Endpoint health checks
CloudWatch alarm health checks
TCP health checks only
questions.correct_rationale: Calculated checks combine the results of child health checks.
questions.distractor_summary: The other types monitor endpoints or alarms directly.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Design solutions that integrate load balancing to meet high availability, scalability, and security requirements
questions.question: An application needs to route requests by host name and path to different microservices and support WebSockets. Which load balancer fits best?
options: Network Load Balancer
Gateway Load Balancer
Classic Load Balancer
Application Load Balancer
questions.correct_rationale: ALBs route at layer 7 by host and path and support WebSockets.
questions.distractor_summary: NLBs work at layer 4, Gateway Load Balancer serves appliances, and Classic is a legacy option.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Design solutions that integrate load balancing to meet high availability, scalability, and security requirements
questions.question: A service requires the client's original source IP at the targets, extreme throughput, and static IPs per AZ. Which design fits best?
options: An Application Load Balancer with X-Forwarded-For only
A Classic Load Balancer with proxy protocol
A Gateway Load Balancer
A Network Load Balancer with Elastic IPs and client IP preservation enabled
questions.correct_rationale: NLBs support Elastic IPs per AZ, very high throughput, and preserve client IPs.
questions.distractor_summary: ALBs do not provide static IPs, Classic is legacy, and Gateway Load Balancer is for appliances.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Design solutions that integrate load balancing to meet high availability, scalability, and security requirements
questions.question: Which load balancer type uses GENEVE encapsulation to send traffic to third-party appliances?
options: Application Load Balancer
Network Load Balancer
Gateway Load Balancer
Classic Load Balancer
questions.correct_rationale: Gateway Load Balancer forwards traffic to virtual appliances with GENEVE.
questions.distractor_summary: The other types do not use GENEVE.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Design solutions that integrate load balancing to meet high availability, scalability, and security requirements
questions.question: An ALB must authenticate users through the corporate OIDC identity provider before requests reach targets. What should be configured?
options: A security group rule
An authenticate-oidc action on the ALB listener rule
A network ACL
An NLB TLS listener
questions.correct_rationale: ALB listener rules can authenticate users with OIDC or Cognito.
questions.distractor_summary: Security groups and ACLs do not authenticate users, and NLBs do not support this action.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Design solutions that integrate load balancing to meet high availability, scalability, and security requirements
questions.question: A company needs to expose a TCP service privately to other VPCs and accounts without peering. Which design fits best?
options: A Network Load Balancer as an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service, consumed through interface endpoints
A public ALB with security group restrictions
VPC peering between all consumers
A NAT gateway shared across VPCs
questions.correct_rationale: PrivateLink exposes services privately with consumer-side interface endpoints.
questions.distractor_summary: Public ALBs use the internet, peering exposes full networks, and NAT gateways do not publish services.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Design solutions that integrate load balancing to meet high availability, scalability, and security requirements
questions.question: Which ALB feature lets traffic be split between two target groups by weight?
options: Weighted target groups in a forward action
Cross-zone load balancing
Deregistration delay
Slow start mode
questions.correct_rationale: Weighted forwarding splits traffic across target groups, useful for blue/green.
questions.distractor_summary: The other features control distribution, draining, and ramp-up.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Design solutions that integrate load balancing to meet high availability, scalability, and security requirements
questions.question: Targets need time to warm up caches before receiving full traffic after registration. Which ALB feature helps?
options: Sticky sessions
Deregistration delay
HTTP/2 to targets
Slow start mode on the target group
questions.correct_rationale: Slow start ramps traffic to newly registered targets over a set period.
questions.distractor_summary: Sticky sessions keep users on targets, deregistration delay drains old targets, and HTTP/2 is a protocol choice.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Design solutions that integrate load balancing to meet high availability, scalability, and security requirements
questions.question: An NLB fronts a TLS application. The company wants TLS terminated at the NLB with certificates from ACM, while targets receive plain TCP within the VPC. What should be configured?
options: An HTTPS listener on the NLB
A TCP listener with the certificate installed only on the NLB subnet
A TLS listener on the NLB with an ACM certificate and TCP target groups
An ALB with UDP listeners
questions.correct_rationale: NLBs support TLS listeners that terminate TLS and forward TCP to targets.
questions.distractor_summary: NLBs do not have HTTPS listeners, certificates are not placed on subnets, and ALBs do not support UDP.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Design solutions that integrate load balancing to meet high availability, scalability, and security requirements
questions.question: What happens when cross-zone load balancing is disabled on a Network Load Balancer?
options: Traffic is blocked between AZs
Each load balancer node distributes traffic only to targets in its own Availability Zone
The NLB becomes Regional only for one AZ
Health checks stop working
questions.correct_rationale: Without cross-zone, nodes send traffic only to targets in their AZ, which can cause imbalance if targets are uneven.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not block inter-AZ traffic, limit to one AZ, or stop health checks.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Design solutions that integrate load balancing to meet high availability, scalability, and security requirements
questions.question: An internal application must be reached by on-premises clients over Direct Connect through a load balancer with a fixed IP for firewall rules. What fits best?
options: A public ALB
An internal Network Load Balancer with static private IPs per subnet
A Classic Load Balancer with dynamic IPs
CloudFront
questions.correct_rationale: Internal NLBs can use specified private IPs, which simplifies on-premises firewall rules.
questions.distractor_summary: Public ALBs are internet-facing, ALBs and Classic use changing IPs, and CloudFront is public.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Define logging and monitoring requirements across AWS and hybrid networks
questions.question: A network team must capture metadata for all traffic in a VPC, including rejected packets, for security analysis. What should be enabled?
options: VPC Flow Logs with traffic type ALL
CloudTrail management events
ALB access logs only
Route 53 query logging
questions.correct_rationale: Flow Logs with ALL capture accepted and rejected traffic metadata.
questions.distractor_summary: CloudTrail records APIs, ALB logs cover only load balancer requests, and query logs cover DNS.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Define logging and monitoring requirements across AWS and hybrid networks
questions.question: Which Flow Logs custom field shows the AWS service associated with traffic, such as S3 or EC2?
options: action
log-status
account-id
pkt-src-aws-service and pkt-dst-aws-service
questions.correct_rationale: These fields identify the AWS service of the packet source or destination.
questions.distractor_summary: The other fields show the action, logging status, and account.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Define logging and monitoring requirements across AWS and hybrid networks
questions.question: Network performance between on premises and AWS over Direct Connect must be monitored, including BGP status and data rates, with alarms. What should be used?
options: AWS Artifact reports
S3 server access logs
CloudWatch metrics for Direct Connect, such as ConnectionState, ConnectionBpsEgress, and virtual interface BGP status
IAM Access Analyzer
questions.correct_rationale: Direct Connect publishes connection and VIF metrics in CloudWatch for alarms.
questions.distractor_summary: The other tools do not monitor Direct Connect.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Define logging and monitoring requirements across AWS and hybrid networks
questions.question: Which service measures packet loss and latency between AWS Regions and Availability Zones to help diagnose AWS network impact?
options: AWS Config
AWS Budgets
AWS Network Manager Infrastructure Performance
Amazon Macie
questions.correct_rationale: Infrastructure Performance shows AWS network latency and packet loss metrics.
questions.distractor_summary: The other services do not measure network performance.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Define logging and monitoring requirements across AWS and hybrid networks
questions.question: Hybrid application owners want end-to-end visibility of network paths and latency between on-premises sites and AWS. Which feature helps?
options: AWS Trusted Advisor service limits
CloudWatch Network Monitor (synthetic probes from AWS to on-premises destinations)
S3 Storage Lens
AWS Cost Explorer
questions.correct_rationale: Network Monitor sends probes over hybrid connections and reports latency and loss.
questions.distractor_summary: The other tools do not monitor hybrid paths.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Define logging and monitoring requirements across AWS and hybrid networks
questions.question: A company needs centralized visibility of Transit Gateways, their attachments, and route changes across Regions. Which service fits best?
options: AWS Cloud WAN or AWS Network Manager with Transit Gateway network registration, including route analysis and events
Amazon Inspector
AWS Artifact
Amazon QuickSight alone
questions.correct_rationale: Network Manager provides a global view, events, and route analysis for registered networks.
questions.distractor_summary: Inspector, Artifact, and QuickSight do not monitor network topology.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Define logging and monitoring requirements across AWS and hybrid networks
questions.question: Which Transit Gateway feature captures metadata about traffic flowing through the Transit Gateway?
options: Transit Gateway route tables
Transit Gateway Connect attachments
Transit Gateway multicast domains
Transit Gateway Flow Logs
questions.correct_rationale: Transit Gateway Flow Logs record traffic metadata at the Transit Gateway.
questions.distractor_summary: Route tables, Connect attachments, and multicast domains do not log traffic.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Define logging and monitoring requirements across AWS and hybrid networks
questions.question: A company wants to analyze VPC Flow Logs cheaply with SQL over months of data. What fits best?
options: Keep logs in CloudWatch Logs forever
Download logs to a laptop
Store logs on EBS volumes
Deliver Flow Logs to S3 in Parquet with hourly partitions and query them with Athena
questions.correct_rationale: S3 with Parquet and partitions is cheap and efficient for Athena queries.
questions.distractor_summary: Long CloudWatch retention is costly, and laptops and EBS are not analysis platforms.

questions.subdomain: 1.5 Design a routing strategy and connectivity architecture between on-premises networks and the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A company needs a hybrid connection with consistent latency and 10 Gbps bandwidth, and the traffic must not traverse the public internet. What fits best?
options: AWS Site-to-Site VPN over the internet
AWS Client VPN
AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection
VPC peering
questions.correct_rationale: Direct Connect provides private, consistent connectivity at high bandwidth.
questions.distractor_summary: VPNs use the internet, Client VPN is for users, and peering connects VPCs.

questions.subdomain: 1.5 Design a routing strategy and connectivity architecture between on-premises networks and the AWS Cloud
questions.question: For maximum resiliency for critical workloads, what Direct Connect topology does AWS recommend?
options: One connection with two virtual interfaces
Separate connections terminating on separate devices in more than one Direct Connect location
Two connections on the same device at one location
One connection with a VPN backup over the same circuit
questions.correct_rationale: Multiple locations and devices protect against device, connection, and location failures.
questions.distractor_summary: Multiple VIFs or connections on one device or location share the same failure points.

questions.subdomain: 1.5 Design a routing strategy and connectivity architecture between on-premises networks and the AWS Cloud
questions.question: Which Direct Connect virtual interface type is used to connect to a Transit Gateway through a Direct Connect gateway?
options: Transit virtual interface
Private virtual interface
Public virtual interface
Hosted connection only
questions.correct_rationale: Transit VIFs connect a Direct Connect gateway to Transit Gateways.
questions.distractor_summary: Private VIFs connect to virtual private gateways, and public VIFs reach public AWS endpoints.

questions.subdomain: 1.5 Design a routing strategy and connectivity architecture between on-premises networks and the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A company has Direct Connect as its primary link and a Site-to-Site VPN as backup. How can it ensure traffic prefers Direct Connect?
options: AWS prefers Direct Connect routes over VPN routes for the same prefix; also advertise more specific prefixes or use BGP attributes as needed
Set a higher MTU on the VPN
Remove the VPN
Use static routes on the VPN with longer prefixes than Direct Connect
questions.correct_rationale: AWS route selection prefers Direct Connect for identical prefixes, and BGP tuning can reinforce it.
questions.distractor_summary: MTU does not affect path choice, removing the VPN loses backup, and longer VPN prefixes would attract traffic to the VPN.

questions.subdomain: 1.5 Design a routing strategy and connectivity architecture between on-premises networks and the AWS Cloud
questions.question: On-premises routers advertise 200 prefixes to a VPC through a private VIF, but routes are not accepted. What is a likely cause?
options: The VPC has too many subnets
MTU is set to 1500
The VIF uses VLAN tagging
The number of advertised routes exceeds the limit for a private virtual interface (100 routes), which causes the BGP session to go down
questions.correct_rationale: Exceeding the prefix limit on a VIF brings the BGP session down; summarize routes to stay within limits.
questions.distractor_summary: Subnet count, MTU, and VLAN tagging do not cause this.

questions.subdomain: 1.5 Design a routing strategy and connectivity architecture between on-premises networks and the AWS Cloud
questions.question: Which BGP attribute can on-premises routers set on routes advertised to AWS to influence which Direct Connect connection AWS uses for return traffic?
options: MED values on AWS side only
TTL
AS_PATH prepending (or local preference communities from AWS)
DSCP
questions.correct_rationale: AS_PATH prepending makes a path less preferred, and AWS local preference communities also influence outbound routing from AWS.
questions.distractor_summary: TTL and DSCP are not BGP path attributes, and MED alone is less reliable across locations.

questions.subdomain: 1.5 Design a routing strategy and connectivity architecture between on-premises networks and the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A company needs hybrid connectivity quickly while Direct Connect is provisioned. What is the best interim option?
options: Wait for Direct Connect before migrating anything
AWS Site-to-Site VPN to a virtual private gateway or Transit Gateway
Use public IPs for all traffic without encryption
Use VPC peering to on premises
questions.correct_rationale: Site-to-Site VPN can be set up in minutes and provides encrypted connectivity.
questions.distractor_summary: Waiting delays projects, unencrypted public traffic is risky, and peering does not connect to on premises.

questions.subdomain: 1.5 Design a routing strategy and connectivity architecture between on-premises networks and the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A Site-to-Site VPN must provide higher throughput than a single tunnel's limit. What design fits best?
options: Use a virtual private gateway with ECMP
Use Transit Gateway with multiple VPN connections and ECMP enabled
Increase the MTU to 9001 on the VPN
Use a single VPN tunnel with a larger instance
questions.correct_rationale: Transit Gateway supports ECMP across multiple VPN tunnels to aggregate bandwidth.
questions.distractor_summary: Virtual private gateways do not support ECMP across VPNs, VPN MTU is limited, and tunnel throughput is not tied to instance size.

questions.subdomain: 1.6 Design a routing strategy and connectivity architecture that include multiple AWS accounts, AWS Regions, and VPCs to support different connectivity patterns
questions.question: A company has 60 VPCs across 20 accounts that all need to reach each other and a shared services VPC. The team wants to avoid managing a full mesh of peering connections. What design fits best?
options: A Transit Gateway shared through AWS Resource Access Manager, with each VPC attached to it
A full mesh of VPC peering connections
One Site-to-Site VPN per VPC to a central EC2 router
A NAT gateway in each VPC pointing at the shared services VPC
questions.correct_rationale: A Transit Gateway acts as a regional hub, and RAM sharing lets attachments come from many accounts, which replaces a mesh of peering connections.
questions.distractor_summary: A peering mesh grows quadratically, per-VPC VPNs to an EC2 router add a single point of failure and operational load, and NAT gateways do not route between VPCs.

questions.subdomain: 1.6 Design a routing strategy and connectivity architecture that include multiple AWS accounts, AWS Regions, and VPCs to support different connectivity patterns
questions.question: Development VPCs must reach shared services but must never reach production VPCs, even though all of them attach to one Transit Gateway. What should the network team design?
options: One default Transit Gateway route table with all attachments associated and propagated
Security groups in shared services that reference development security groups across the Transit Gateway
VPC peering between development and production with deny rules in route tables
Separate Transit Gateway route tables for development, production, and shared services, with associations and propagations that only allow the permitted paths
questions.correct_rationale: Multiple Transit Gateway route tables provide routing domains, so development routes reach shared services but have no path to production.
questions.distractor_summary: A single default table allows everything to reach everything, security groups cannot reference groups across a Transit Gateway, and route tables have no deny rules.

questions.subdomain: 1.6 Design a routing strategy and connectivity architecture that include multiple AWS accounts, AWS Regions, and VPCs to support different connectivity patterns
questions.question: How are Transit Gateways in two different AWS Regions connected to each other?
options: With a Direct Connect gateway association between the two Transit Gateways
By enabling route propagation between Regions automatically
With a Transit Gateway peering attachment, using static routes that point to the peering attachment
With an interface VPC endpoint in each Region
questions.correct_rationale: Inter-Region Transit Gateway peering uses a peering attachment, and routes to the remote side are added statically.
questions.distractor_summary: A Direct Connect gateway does not link Transit Gateways to each other, propagation does not cross peering attachments, and interface endpoints do not connect Transit Gateways.

questions.subdomain: 1.6 Design a routing strategy and connectivity architecture that include multiple AWS accounts, AWS Regions, and VPCs to support different connectivity patterns
questions.question: A global company wants a managed wide area network across Regions with a single policy document that defines segments such as production and development, and it wants routes shared automatically between Regions. What fits best?
options: Transit Gateways in each Region peered manually with static routes
VPC peering between every pair of VPCs in every Region
AWS Cloud WAN with a core network policy that defines segments and edge locations
A Direct Connect gateway connected to every VPC
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud WAN builds a global core network from a central policy, with segments that keep traffic separated and dynamic routing between Regions.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual Transit Gateway peering needs static routes, global peering meshes do not scale, and a Direct Connect gateway is for hybrid connectivity rather than a managed WAN.

questions.subdomain: 1.6 Design a routing strategy and connectivity architecture that include multiple AWS accounts, AWS Regions, and VPCs to support different connectivity patterns
questions.question: Two VPCs owned by partner companies use the same CIDR range, 10.0.0.0/16. One VPC must expose a single HTTP service to the other. What is the simplest design?
options: Create a VPC peering connection between the two VPCs
Publish the service through an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service, and create an interface endpoint in the consumer VPC
Attach both VPCs to a Transit Gateway and propagate their routes
Change the route tables so each VPC points to the other VPC CIDR
questions.correct_rationale: PrivateLink connects a consumer to a single service through an endpoint with local IP addresses, so overlapping CIDR ranges do not matter.
questions.distractor_summary: Peering and Transit Gateway routing both fail with overlapping CIDR ranges, and route table edits cannot resolve identical prefixes.

questions.subdomain: 1.6 Design a routing strategy and connectivity architecture that include multiple AWS accounts, AWS Regions, and VPCs to support different connectivity patterns
questions.question: Which statement about VPC peering is correct?
options: Peering is not transitive, so VPC A cannot reach VPC C through VPC B
Peering supports overlapping CIDR blocks if both owners accept the request
Peering works only between VPCs in the same Region
Peering requires an internet gateway in both VPCs
questions.correct_rationale: VPC peering is a one-to-one relationship with no transitive routing through an intermediate VPC.
questions.distractor_summary: Overlapping CIDR blocks are not allowed, inter-Region peering is supported, and peering needs no internet gateway.

questions.subdomain: 1.6 Design a routing strategy and connectivity architecture that include multiple AWS accounts, AWS Regions, and VPCs to support different connectivity patterns
questions.question: A company wants to centralize outbound internet access for 40 VPCs to cut NAT gateway costs and inspect traffic in one place. What design fits best?
options: An internet gateway in every VPC with security groups blocking inbound traffic
VPC peering from every spoke to one VPC that has an internet gateway
A gateway VPC endpoint for the internet in each spoke
An egress VPC with NAT gateways attached to a Transit Gateway, with spoke VPC default routes pointing to the Transit Gateway
questions.correct_rationale: A centralized egress VPC behind a Transit Gateway shares NAT gateways and gives one place to inspect outbound traffic.
questions.distractor_summary: Per-VPC internet gateways do not centralize anything, peering does not allow edge-to-edge routing through an internet gateway, and gateway endpoints serve only S3 and DynamoDB.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement routing and connectivity between on-premises networks and the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A network engineer is creating a Site-to-Site VPN to a virtual private gateway. Which resource represents the on-premises router in AWS?
options: A carrier gateway
An egress-only internet gateway
A Direct Connect location
A customer gateway with the router's public IP address and BGP ASN
questions.correct_rationale: The customer gateway resource records the on-premises device's public IP address and, for dynamic routing, its BGP ASN.
questions.distractor_summary: Carrier gateways serve Wavelength Zones, egress-only gateways are for IPv6 outbound traffic, and Direct Connect locations are physical facilities.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement routing and connectivity between on-premises networks and the AWS Cloud
questions.question: Routes learned over a Site-to-Site VPN attached to a virtual private gateway are not appearing in a subnet route table. What should the engineer check first?
options: Whether the subnet has an internet gateway route
Whether the VPN tunnels use IKEv1
Whether route propagation from the virtual private gateway is enabled on that route table
Whether the VPC has DNS hostnames enabled
questions.correct_rationale: Learned routes reach a subnet route table only when propagation from the virtual private gateway is enabled or static routes are added.
questions.distractor_summary: An internet gateway route, the IKE version, and DNS settings do not control route propagation.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement routing and connectivity between on-premises networks and the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A company has a Direct Connect connection and must reach VPCs in three Regions through a single private connection without creating separate virtual interfaces for each VPC. What should be implemented?
options: A public virtual interface per Region
A Direct Connect gateway associated with Transit Gateways or virtual private gateways in each Region, reached through one virtual interface
A separate private virtual interface for each VPC in each Region
VPC peering from the Direct Connect location to each Region
questions.correct_rationale: A Direct Connect gateway is a global object that lets one virtual interface reach gateways in many Regions.
questions.distractor_summary: Public VIFs reach public endpoints, one VIF per VPC is what the company wants to avoid, and peering does not terminate at a Direct Connect location.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement routing and connectivity between on-premises networks and the AWS Cloud
questions.question: Which BGP ASN range can be used for the AWS side of a virtual private gateway when the default is not wanted?
options: A private ASN, in the 64512 to 65534 range or the 4200000000 to 4294967294 range
Only ASN 7224
Any public ASN, without proof of ownership
ASN 0
questions.correct_rationale: Custom Amazon-side ASNs are private ASNs from the 16-bit or 32-bit private ranges.
questions.distractor_summary: 7224 is only one default value, public ASNs need ownership, and ASN 0 is reserved.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement routing and connectivity between on-premises networks and the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A company must encrypt all traffic over its Direct Connect connection at layer 2 between its router and the AWS device. Which option fits?
options: MACsec on a supported dedicated connection
IPsec on a public virtual interface
TLS on the BGP session
Encryption using AWS KMS on the virtual interface
questions.correct_rationale: MACsec gives point-to-point layer 2 encryption on supported dedicated Direct Connect connections.
questions.distractor_summary: IPsec over a public VIF is a different layer and design, BGP sessions do not use TLS for data, and KMS does not encrypt link traffic.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement routing and connectivity between on-premises networks and the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A company wants an IPsec VPN over its Direct Connect link so that traffic is encrypted but does not traverse the public internet. What should be configured?
options: A client VPN endpoint over a public VIF
A VPC peering connection over Direct Connect
An internet gateway attached to a Direct Connect gateway
A Site-to-Site VPN to a Transit Gateway using private IP addresses over a transit virtual interface
questions.correct_rationale: Private IP VPN over Direct Connect uses a transit virtual interface and Transit Gateway so IPsec runs privately over the dedicated link.
questions.distractor_summary: Client VPN serves individual users, peering does not run over Direct Connect, and internet gateways cannot attach to a Direct Connect gateway.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement routing and connectivity between on-premises networks and the AWS Cloud
questions.question: What does enabling Bidirectional Forwarding Detection on a Direct Connect virtual interface provide?
options: Encryption of BGP routing updates
Automatic increase of the link bandwidth
Faster detection of a failed link so BGP can fail over quickly
Route summarization at the AWS edge
questions.correct_rationale: BFD detects path failures in a sub-second time frame, which speeds up BGP failover compared with hold timers alone.
questions.distractor_summary: BFD does not encrypt, scale bandwidth, or summarize routes.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement routing and connectivity between on-premises networks and the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A company has two Direct Connect connections in different locations to the same Direct Connect gateway. It wants AWS to prefer the first connection for traffic going back to on premises. What is the most reliable method?
options: Set a lower MTU on the second connection
Tag the advertised prefixes with the AWS local preference BGP community that gives the first connection a higher preference
Advertise more specific prefixes over both connections equally
Disable route propagation on the second virtual interface
questions.correct_rationale: AWS honors local preference communities on prefixes received over Direct Connect, which controls the path chosen for return traffic.
questions.distractor_summary: MTU does not change path selection, equal advertisements do not set a preference, and disabling propagation does not apply to virtual interfaces this way.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement routing and connectivity between on-premises networks and the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A Site-to-Site VPN tunnel goes down whenever there is no traffic for a while. What change can keep the tunnel up?
options: Increase the VPC CIDR range
Configure dead peer detection and keep traffic flowing, or set the tunnel startup action and DPD timeout action appropriately
Disable BGP on the tunnel
Remove the customer gateway and recreate it daily
questions.correct_rationale: DPD settings and tunnel options control idle behavior, and steady keepalive traffic or a restart action keeps the tunnel established.
questions.distractor_summary: CIDR size, removing BGP, and recreating the customer gateway do not address idle timeouts.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement routing and connectivity between on-premises networks and the AWS Cloud
questions.question: What is the maximum transmission unit supported for traffic sent over a Site-to-Site VPN tunnel?
options: About 1446 bytes, because IPsec encapsulation adds overhead
9001 bytes
8500 bytes
65535 bytes
questions.correct_rationale: IPsec headers reduce the usable MTU through a VPN tunnel to roughly 1446 bytes, so applications should allow for this.
questions.distractor_summary: 9001 bytes is the in-VPC jumbo frame size, 8500 applies to some Direct Connect and Transit Gateway paths, and 65535 is not a link MTU.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement routing and connectivity between on-premises networks and the AWS Cloud
questions.question: Jumbo frames must be used for traffic between an on-premises data center and a VPC over Direct Connect through a Transit Gateway. What MTU should be configured?
options: 9001 bytes end to end
1500 bytes because Direct Connect does not support jumbo frames
1446 bytes to match VPN overhead
8500 bytes on the transit virtual interface and the on-premises router
questions.correct_rationale: Transit virtual interfaces and Transit Gateway support jumbo frames up to 8500 bytes, so both ends should match.
questions.distractor_summary: 9001 exceeds what the Transit Gateway path supports, Direct Connect does support jumbo frames, and 1446 is the VPN limit.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement routing and connectivity between on-premises networks and the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A company has 90 on-premises prefixes but must stay below the route limit for a private virtual interface. What should the network team do?
options: Advertise a default route from AWS to on premises
Add a second VPC
Summarize the on-premises prefixes into fewer, larger CIDR blocks before advertising them
Switch to static routing on the virtual interface
questions.correct_rationale: Route summarization reduces the number of advertised prefixes so the session stays under the limit.
questions.distractor_summary: A default route from AWS does not reduce inbound prefixes, a second VPC changes nothing, and Direct Connect VIFs use BGP.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement routing and connectivity between on-premises networks and the AWS Cloud
questions.question: When a Direct Connect connection and a Site-to-Site VPN both advertise the same prefix to a virtual private gateway, which path does AWS prefer by default?
options: The VPN path, because it is encrypted
Whichever path was created first
The Direct Connect path
Traffic is always split evenly between them
questions.correct_rationale: For identical prefixes, AWS prefers Direct Connect BGP routes over VPN routes.
questions.distractor_summary: Encryption, creation order, and even splitting do not decide the default preference.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement routing and connectivity between on-premises networks and the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A company uses an AWS Site-to-Site VPN with static routing and two tunnels. Failover to the second tunnel is slow and sometimes traffic is dropped asymmetrically. What change improves this?
options: Delete the second tunnel
Use dynamic routing with BGP on both tunnels so routes fail over automatically
Increase the instance size in the VPC
Disable route propagation on the subnet route table
questions.correct_rationale: BGP lets each tunnel advertise and withdraw routes, so failover is automatic and symmetric.
questions.distractor_summary: Removing redundancy makes outages worse, instance size has no effect on the tunnel, and disabling propagation removes learned routes.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Implement routing and connectivity between on-premises networks and the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A small branch office must connect to AWS quickly with an IPsec tunnel, and the company has no hardware VPN appliance. What option fits?
options: Run a software VPN appliance or use a supported router, and create a Site-to-Site VPN to the Transit Gateway
Order a dedicated Direct Connect connection for the branch
Create a VPC peering connection to the branch
Use a gateway VPC endpoint for the branch
questions.correct_rationale: A software or supported router can terminate the Site-to-Site VPN tunnels quickly without a dedicated appliance.
questions.distractor_summary: Direct Connect takes longer to provision, peering connects VPCs only, and gateway endpoints serve S3 and DynamoDB.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement routing and connectivity across multiple AWS accounts, Regions, and VPCs to support different connectivity patterns
questions.question: A network account owns a Transit Gateway. Application accounts must attach their VPCs to it. What should the network team do?
options: Copy the Transit Gateway into each application account
Create IAM users in the network account for each application team
Use VPC peering between the network account and each application account
Share the Transit Gateway with the application accounts or the organization through AWS Resource Access Manager
questions.correct_rationale: RAM sharing lets other accounts create attachments to the Transit Gateway owned by the network account.
questions.distractor_summary: Transit Gateways cannot be copied, IAM users are not how cross-account attachments work, and peering does not create Transit Gateway attachments.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement routing and connectivity across multiple AWS accounts, Regions, and VPCs to support different connectivity patterns
questions.question: New VPC attachments to a shared Transit Gateway should not be connected automatically to existing routing domains. What setting should be changed?
options: Disable DNS support on the Transit Gateway
Enable auto accept shared attachments
Enable multicast support
Disable default route table association and default route table propagation on the Transit Gateway
questions.correct_rationale: With default association and propagation disabled, new attachments have no routes until the team associates them with the right route table.
questions.distractor_summary: DNS support and multicast are unrelated, and auto accept makes attachments join faster rather than isolating them.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement routing and connectivity across multiple AWS accounts, Regions, and VPCs to support different connectivity patterns
questions.question: In a Transit Gateway, what is the difference between associating and propagating an attachment?
options: Association advertises routes, and propagation accepts the attachment
They are the same operation with different names
Association sets which route table is used for traffic from the attachment, and propagation installs the attachment's routes into a route table
Association applies only to VPN attachments, and propagation only to VPC attachments
questions.correct_rationale: Each attachment is associated with one route table for lookups, while it can propagate routes into one or more route tables.
questions.distractor_summary: The definitions are reversed or merged in the other choices, and both operations apply to all attachment types.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement routing and connectivity across multiple AWS accounts, Regions, and VPCs to support different connectivity patterns
questions.question: Traffic between VPCs on a Transit Gateway must pass through a firewall in an inspection VPC, and the firewall must see both directions of each flow. What setting should be enabled on the inspection VPC attachment?
options: Default route table propagation
Appliance mode
DNS support
IPv6 support only
questions.correct_rationale: Appliance mode keeps both directions of a flow in the same Availability Zone, so a stateful firewall sees symmetric traffic.
questions.distractor_summary: Propagation, DNS support, and IPv6 settings do not make traffic symmetric through the appliance.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement routing and connectivity across multiple AWS accounts, Regions, and VPCs to support different connectivity patterns
questions.question: Two VPCs in different Regions must exchange data privately with low operational overhead, and there are only two VPCs involved. What is the simplest option?
options: An inter-Region VPC peering connection with routes in both VPCs
A Transit Gateway in each Region with a peering attachment
A Site-to-Site VPN between two EC2 instances
A Direct Connect connection between the two Regions
questions.correct_rationale: For two VPCs, inter-Region peering is simple, private, and encrypted on the AWS backbone.
questions.distractor_summary: Transit Gateways add cost and parts for just two VPCs, EC2 VPNs add operational load, and Direct Connect is for on-premises connectivity.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement routing and connectivity across multiple AWS accounts, Regions, and VPCs to support different connectivity patterns
questions.question: A company uses AWS Cloud WAN. Traffic between the production and development segments must be allowed only for a shared logging service. How can this be done?
options: Use segment actions in the core network policy to share specific routes between the segments
Merge the two segments into one
Add a security group rule to the core network
Create VPC peering from every production VPC to every development VPC
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud WAN segment sharing in the policy controls which routes are visible between segments.
questions.distractor_summary: Merging segments removes isolation, core networks do not use security groups, and peering bypasses Cloud WAN.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement routing and connectivity across multiple AWS accounts, Regions, and VPCs to support different connectivity patterns
questions.question: Which feature lets a VPC owner share subnets with other accounts so their resources run in the same VPC?
options: VPC peering
AWS PrivateLink
Transit Gateway Connect
VPC sharing through AWS Resource Access Manager
questions.correct_rationale: VPC sharing lets participant accounts launch resources into subnets owned by another account.
questions.distractor_summary: Peering connects two VPCs, PrivateLink exposes a service, and Transit Gateway Connect attaches SD-WAN appliances.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement routing and connectivity across multiple AWS accounts, Regions, and VPCs to support different connectivity patterns
questions.question: A company uses SD-WAN appliances in a VPC and wants them to exchange routes dynamically with a Transit Gateway using GRE tunnels and BGP. Which feature fits?
options: A VPN attachment with static routes
VPC peering with the appliance VPC
A Transit Gateway Connect attachment
A Gateway Load Balancer endpoint
questions.correct_rationale: Transit Gateway Connect uses GRE and BGP for SD-WAN appliances and offers more bandwidth than IPsec VPN.
questions.distractor_summary: Static VPN routes are not dynamic, peering does not exchange BGP routes, and Gateway Load Balancer is for inspection.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement routing and connectivity across multiple AWS accounts, Regions, and VPCs to support different connectivity patterns
questions.question: VPC A and VPC B are peered. Instances in VPC A cannot reach instances in VPC B, even though the peering connection is active. What should be checked first?
options: Whether VPC B has a NAT gateway
Route table entries in both VPCs that point to the peering connection for the other CIDR
Whether Route 53 health checks are enabled
Whether the VPCs share the same account
questions.correct_rationale: Peering requires routes in each VPC that send the remote CIDR to the peering connection, plus security rules that allow the traffic.
questions.distractor_summary: NAT gateways and health checks are unrelated, and peering works across accounts.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement routing and connectivity across multiple AWS accounts, Regions, and VPCs to support different connectivity patterns
questions.question: Which AWS feature supports multicast traffic between EC2 instances across VPCs?
options: VPC peering with multicast enabled
Transit Gateway multicast domains
Elastic Load Balancing
AWS Global Accelerator
questions.correct_rationale: A Transit Gateway with multicast support uses multicast domains to deliver multicast traffic between members.
questions.distractor_summary: Peering does not support multicast, and load balancers and Global Accelerator do not deliver multicast.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement routing and connectivity across multiple AWS accounts, Regions, and VPCs to support different connectivity patterns
questions.question: A company needs a VPC in one account to reach a fleet of databases behind an NLB in another account. The CIDR blocks overlap, and the producer must approve each consumer. What should be implemented?
options: An endpoint service backed by the NLB with acceptance required, and an interface endpoint in the consumer VPC
VPC peering with route filters
A Transit Gateway with static routes for the overlapping ranges
An internet-facing NLB with security group rules
questions.correct_rationale: PrivateLink endpoint services can require acceptance, and they work with overlapping CIDR ranges.
questions.distractor_summary: Peering and Transit Gateway routing fail with overlap, and an internet-facing NLB exposes the service publicly.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement routing and connectivity across multiple AWS accounts, Regions, and VPCs to support different connectivity patterns
questions.question: Two VPCs on the same Transit Gateway can ping each other, but traffic to a third VPC fails. The third VPC's attachment is associated with the correct route table. What is the most likely cause?
options: The Transit Gateway has reached its bandwidth limit
DNS support is disabled on the VPC
The VPC has an IPv6 CIDR block
The third VPC's routes are not propagated into the route table used by the other attachments, or its subnet route tables lack a route to the Transit Gateway
questions.correct_rationale: Both directions need routes: in the Transit Gateway route tables and in each VPC's subnet route tables.
questions.distractor_summary: Bandwidth limits do not cause total loss for one VPC, DNS settings do not block ping by IP, and IPv6 does not block IPv4 traffic.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Implement routing and connectivity across multiple AWS accounts, Regions, and VPCs to support different connectivity patterns
questions.question: What is a Transit Gateway blackhole route used for?
options: Forwarding all unknown traffic to an internet gateway
Logging traffic to CloudWatch
Dropping traffic that matches a specific destination CIDR
Load balancing traffic across attachments
questions.correct_rationale: A blackhole route drops matching traffic, which is useful for blocking paths in a routing domain.
questions.distractor_summary: Blackhole routes do not forward, log, or balance traffic.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Implement complex hybrid and multi-account DNS architectures
questions.question: On-premises applications must resolve names in a Route 53 private hosted zone. What should be created in the VPC?
options: A Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint only
A public hosted zone with the same name
A Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint, and on-premises DNS servers configured to forward the zone to its IP addresses
An internet gateway with DNS enabled
questions.correct_rationale: Inbound endpoints accept queries from on premises and resolve them against private hosted zones associated with the VPC.
questions.distractor_summary: Outbound endpoints send queries from AWS to on premises, a public zone exposes records publicly, and internet gateways do not resolve DNS.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Implement complex hybrid and multi-account DNS architectures
questions.question: Many accounts in an organization must use the same Resolver forwarding rules for corp.example.com. What is the most efficient implementation?
options: Create duplicate rules and outbound endpoints in every account
Create the rules in a central networking account, share them through AWS RAM, and associate them with VPCs in each account
Run BIND servers on EC2 in every VPC
Use a public hosted zone for corp.example.com
questions.correct_rationale: Shared Resolver rules let one set of outbound endpoints and rules serve VPCs in many accounts.
questions.distractor_summary: Duplicates increase cost and drift, BIND fleets add operational load, and a public zone exposes internal names.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Implement complex hybrid and multi-account DNS architectures
questions.question: Which Route 53 Resolver rule type tells Resolver to answer a domain itself instead of forwarding it, overriding a broader forwarding rule?
options: A system rule
A forward rule
A recursive rule
A delegation rule only
questions.correct_rationale: System rules make Resolver handle a subdomain locally, even when a broader forward rule exists for the parent domain.
questions.distractor_summary: Forward rules send queries elsewhere, and the other names describe no matching rule type in this scenario.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Implement complex hybrid and multi-account DNS architectures
questions.question: A private hosted zone in a shared services account must be used by VPCs in workload accounts. What steps are needed?
options: Share the hosted zone through AWS RAM only
Copy the zone into each workload account
Make the private hosted zone public
Create a VPC association authorization in the zone owner account, then associate the VPC from the workload account
questions.correct_rationale: Cross-account associations need an authorization from the zone owner followed by an association request from the VPC owner.
questions.distractor_summary: Private hosted zones are not shared through RAM for this purpose, copies drift, and making the zone public exposes it.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Implement complex hybrid and multi-account DNS architectures
questions.question: Resolver query logs from all VPCs in an organization must be sent to a central location. What should be configured?
options: VPC Flow Logs with DNS fields enabled
CloudTrail data events for Route 53
Route 53 health checks on every VPC
A Resolver query logging configuration shared through AWS RAM and sent to a central S3 bucket or CloudWatch Logs destination
questions.correct_rationale: Query logging configurations can be shared and send DNS query details from associated VPCs to one destination.
questions.distractor_summary: Flow Logs do not capture full DNS query names, CloudTrail logs API calls, and health checks do not log queries.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Implement complex hybrid and multi-account DNS architectures
questions.question: A company wants to block DNS lookups for known malicious domains from all VPCs. What should be implemented?
options: Security groups that deny port 53 outbound
A public hosted zone that overrides bad domains
Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall rule groups with managed domain lists, applied across accounts through AWS Firewall Manager
VPC Flow Logs with alarms
questions.correct_rationale: DNS Firewall filters queries from VPCs by domain list, and Firewall Manager applies rule groups across the organization.
questions.distractor_summary: Blocking port 53 breaks all DNS, a public zone cannot override other domains, and Flow Logs detect rather than block.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Implement complex hybrid and multi-account DNS architectures
questions.question: Which IP addresses does an EC2 instance use by default to reach the Route 53 Resolver?
options: The VPC base CIDR plus two, or 169.254.169.253
The address of the internet gateway
The NAT gateway's private address
questions.correct_rationale: The Amazon-provided DNS server is reachable at the VPC base address plus two and at 169.254.169.253.
questions.distractor_summary: Public resolvers, internet gateways, and NAT gateways are not the default VPC resolver.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Implement complex hybrid and multi-account DNS architectures
questions.question: Hybrid DNS lookups from AWS to an on-premises domain fail. The outbound endpoint and forwarding rule exist. What should be checked?
options: The rule is associated with the VPC, the endpoint security group allows DNS traffic, and routing to the on-premises DNS servers works
The VPC has a public hosted zone
The on-premises servers have an AWS Certificate Manager certificate
The VPC has DNS hostnames disabled
questions.correct_rationale: Forwarding needs the rule associated with the VPC, network paths to the target servers, and security group rules for port 53.
questions.distractor_summary: Public zones and certificates are unrelated, and hostname settings do not stop forwarding.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Implement complex hybrid and multi-account DNS architectures
questions.question: A domain is split: some records live in a Route 53 private hosted zone, and other records with the same domain live on premises. Queries for missing records in the private zone return NXDOMAIN. What is the best fix?
options: Move to distinct subdomains, or forward the specific on-premises names with more specific rules, because a private zone answers authoritatively for its whole name
Enable DNSSEC on the private hosted zone
Add a wildcard record that points to the internet gateway
Lower the TTL on all records
questions.correct_rationale: Route 53 answers for the entire private zone, so missing names do not fall back to on premises unless more specific rules route them.
questions.distractor_summary: DNSSEC, wildcard records to gateways, and TTL changes do not change authoritative behavior.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Automate and configure network infrastructure
questions.question: A network team wants VPCs, subnets, and Transit Gateway attachments to be deployed the same way in every account. What should they use?
options: Manual console steps with a written checklist
One large VPC shared by every account with no templates
AWS Config rules only
CloudFormation StackSets or Terraform modules deployed through a pipeline
questions.correct_rationale: Infrastructure as code deployed through a pipeline gives repeatable, reviewable network builds across accounts.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual steps drift, one shared VPC does not meet every need, and Config detects issues but does not deploy.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Automate and configure network infrastructure
questions.question: IP address ranges must be allocated to new VPCs automatically without overlap across hundreds of accounts. Which service fits?
options: A spreadsheet maintained by the network team
Route 53 Resolver rules
Amazon VPC IP Address Manager with pools shared to the organization
AWS Network Firewall
questions.correct_rationale: VPC IPAM manages pools and allocates non-overlapping CIDR ranges, and it can be used directly by CloudFormation and the VPC API.
questions.distractor_summary: Spreadsheets are error-prone, Resolver rules handle DNS, and Network Firewall filters traffic.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Automate and configure network infrastructure
questions.question: Which CloudFormation feature can deploy the same template to many accounts and Regions in an organization?
options: Change sets
StackSets with service-managed permissions
Nested stacks only
Drift detection
questions.correct_rationale: StackSets deploy stacks to target accounts and Regions, and service-managed permissions work with AWS Organizations.
questions.distractor_summary: Change sets preview changes, nested stacks split templates, and drift detection reports differences.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Automate and configure network infrastructure
questions.question: A team wants to see the changes a CloudFormation update will make to the network before applying it. What should they use?
options: A stack policy
A change set
A deletion policy
A wait condition
questions.correct_rationale: Change sets show proposed resource changes, including replacements, before execution.
questions.distractor_summary: Stack policies protect resources, deletion policies control removal, and wait conditions pause stacks.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Automate and configure network infrastructure
questions.question: An update to a VPC template would replace a subnet that runs production workloads. How can the team prevent that update from accidentally happening?
options: Apply a stack policy that denies updates and replacement on the critical subnet resource
Turn off CloudTrail
Delete the change set after review
Set the subnet's DeletionPolicy to Snapshot
questions.correct_rationale: A stack policy can deny update actions on specific resources, which blocks accidental replacement.
questions.distractor_summary: CloudTrail does not block changes, deleting change sets does not protect resources later, and subnets do not support snapshot deletion policies.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Automate and configure network infrastructure
questions.question: Which service can automatically respond to events such as a new VPC being created, for example by attaching it to a Transit Gateway?
options: Amazon S3 lifecycle rules
AWS Trusted Advisor
Amazon Inspector
Amazon EventBridge triggering an AWS Lambda function or Step Functions workflow
questions.correct_rationale: EventBridge rules match API events and invoke automation that configures new resources.
questions.distractor_summary: S3 lifecycle rules move objects, Trusted Advisor makes recommendations, and Inspector scans for vulnerabilities.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Automate and configure network infrastructure
questions.question: A company wants to deploy network configuration from code with a familiar programming language and type checking. What should it use?
options: The AWS Pricing Calculator
AWS Systems Manager Session Manager
The AWS Cloud Development Kit, which synthesizes CloudFormation templates
Amazon CloudWatch dashboards
questions.correct_rationale: The CDK uses general-purpose languages to define infrastructure that deploys through CloudFormation.
questions.distractor_summary: The other choices estimate cost, open shells, or display metrics.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Automate and configure network infrastructure
questions.question: Network templates fail in some accounts because a hard-coded AMI and Availability Zone names differ. How should the templates be improved?
options: Copy a separate template for each account with fixed values
Remove Availability Zone settings so resources go anywhere
Use parameters, SSM Parameter Store public parameters, and intrinsic functions such as Fn::GetAZs
Run the templates only in one Region
questions.correct_rationale: Parameters and dynamic lookups make templates portable across accounts and Regions.
questions.distractor_summary: Per-account copies drift, removing placement breaks subnet design, and restricting Regions does not solve the problem.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Automate and configure network infrastructure
questions.question: What does CloudFormation drift detection report?
options: Costs that exceed the budget
Differences between the stack's expected configuration and the actual resource configuration
Security vulnerabilities in code
Network latency between Regions
questions.correct_rationale: Drift detection compares deployed resources with the template so manual changes can be found.
questions.distractor_summary: Cost, vulnerabilities, and latency are measured by other services.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Automate and configure network infrastructure
questions.question: Before deployment, the team wants to fail any template that creates a security group allowing 0.0.0.0/0 on SSH. What tool fits?
options: AWS CloudFormation Guard rules, or CloudFormation Hooks, run in the pipeline
AWS Cost Explorer
Amazon Detective
Route 53 Application Recovery Controller
questions.correct_rationale: Guard and Hooks check templates against policy rules before or during deployment.
questions.distractor_summary: Cost Explorer reports spending, Detective investigates findings, and Application Recovery Controller manages failover.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Automate and configure network infrastructure
questions.question: Which AWS Systems Manager capability can run a predefined set of steps, such as updating route tables, with approvals?
options: Patch Manager
Inventory
Session Manager
Automation runbooks
questions.correct_rationale: Automation runbooks run multi-step operational tasks, including optional approval steps.
questions.distractor_summary: Patch Manager patches, Inventory collects metadata, and Session Manager opens shells.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Automate and configure network infrastructure
questions.question: A company manages its network with Terraform. Several engineers run changes at the same time and corrupt state. What should be done?
options: Store state files on each laptop
Commit state files to a public repository
Disable the state file
Use a remote backend such as S3 with state locking
questions.correct_rationale: A remote backend with locking prevents concurrent writes and keeps one shared state.
questions.distractor_summary: Local or public state causes conflicts and exposure, and Terraform cannot work without state.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Automate and configure network infrastructure
questions.question: Thousands of security group rules must be kept consistent across accounts, and noncompliant rules must be fixed automatically. What should be used?
options: A weekly manual audit
Network ACLs in a single account
AWS Firewall Manager security group policies with automatic remediation
AWS Budgets alerts
