questions.correct_rationale: Firewall Manager applies and audits security group policies across accounts and can remediate noncompliant groups.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual audits are slow, a single account's network ACLs do not cover the organization, and Budgets track cost.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Automate and configure network infrastructure
questions.question: What does the Route 53 Resolver endpoint require at creation time?
options: A public IP address in an internet gateway
At least two IP addresses in subnets, preferably in different Availability Zones, and a security group
A Direct Connect connection
A KMS key
questions.correct_rationale: Resolver endpoints use elastic network interfaces in at least two subnets and a security group for DNS traffic.
questions.distractor_summary: Endpoints do not need public IPs, Direct Connect, or KMS keys.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Automate and configure network infrastructure
questions.question: A company wants to validate that a planned change will not break reachability between two resources before applying it. Which tool can analyze configurations without sending traffic?
options: VPC Reachability Analyzer
VPC Traffic Mirroring
CloudWatch Synthetics
AWS X-Ray
questions.correct_rationale: Reachability Analyzer reasons about configuration to show whether a path exists and which component blocks it.
questions.distractor_summary: Traffic Mirroring copies packets, Synthetics sends test traffic, and X-Ray traces application requests.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Maintain routing and connectivity on AWS and hybrid networks
questions.question: After a new on-premises prefix is added, some VPCs reach it and others do not. All VPCs attach to the same Transit Gateway. What is the most likely cause?
options: Some VPC subnet route tables do not have a route for the new prefix pointing to the Transit Gateway
The Transit Gateway reached its attachment limit
The new prefix is advertised with too short an AS path
DNS hostnames are disabled in the failing VPCs
questions.correct_rationale: Transit Gateway routes only help if each VPC's subnet route tables also send the prefix to the Transit Gateway.
questions.distractor_summary: An attachment limit would block new attachments, AS path length affects path choice rather than reachability, and DNS settings do not affect routing by IP.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Maintain routing and connectivity on AWS and hybrid networks
questions.question: A company replaces an on-premises router. After the change, the Direct Connect BGP session will not establish. What should the engineer verify?
options: The VPC has an internet gateway
The Transit Gateway has DNS support enabled
The new router uses jumbo frames
The BGP ASN, peer IP addresses, VLAN ID, and MD5 authentication key match the virtual interface configuration
questions.correct_rationale: A BGP session over Direct Connect requires matching VLAN, addressing, ASN, and authentication settings.
questions.distractor_summary: Internet gateways and DNS support are unrelated, and the MTU does not stop the session from forming.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Maintain routing and connectivity on AWS and hybrid networks
questions.question: What is the effect of a more specific route in a VPC route table when a less specific route also matches?
options: The route created first is used
Traffic is split across both routes
The most specific route, the longest prefix match, is used
The less specific route always wins if it points to a Transit Gateway
questions.correct_rationale: VPC routing uses longest prefix match to choose among matching routes.
questions.distractor_summary: Creation order, splitting, and target type do not override longest prefix match.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Maintain routing and connectivity on AWS and hybrid networks
questions.question: A company must move a VPC attachment from one Transit Gateway route table to another with minimal disruption. What is the correct process?
options: Delete the VPC and recreate it
Disassociate the attachment from the current route table and associate it with the new one, after confirming the new table has the needed routes
Detach the VPC from the Transit Gateway permanently
Change the VPC CIDR range
questions.correct_rationale: An attachment can be associated with only one route table, so it is moved by disassociating and reassociating after the target is ready.
questions.distractor_summary: Recreating or detaching the VPC and changing its CIDR range cause far more disruption.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Maintain routing and connectivity on AWS and hybrid networks
questions.question: Overlapping routes from Direct Connect and a VPN cause asymmetric routing: traffic leaves AWS over Direct Connect but returns over the VPN. What should be done?
options: Disable the VPN entirely
Make the on-premises router prefer Direct Connect for return traffic, for example by using local preference on premises and AS path prepending on the VPN
Increase the VPN tunnel MTU
Add a NAT gateway in the VPC
questions.correct_rationale: Path preferences must align on both sides so each flow uses the same link in both directions.
questions.distractor_summary: Removing the backup loses resilience, MTU does not change path selection, and NAT gateways do not fix hybrid asymmetry.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Maintain routing and connectivity on AWS and hybrid networks
questions.question: What does Route 53 Application Recovery Controller provide for multi-Region networks?
options: Readiness checks and routing controls to shift traffic between Regions during recovery
Packet capture between Regions
Automatic VPC peering across Regions
DNS query logging only
questions.correct_rationale: Application Recovery Controller checks recovery readiness and offers highly available routing controls for failover.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not capture packets, create peering, or only log queries.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Maintain routing and connectivity on AWS and hybrid networks
questions.question: A Site-to-Site VPN tunnel shows status DOWN, and the customer gateway logs show phase 1 negotiation failures. What should be checked?
options: The VPC route table propagation setting
The subnet's network ACL for port 443
The Transit Gateway route table association
The IKE version, encryption and integrity algorithms, Diffie-Hellman groups, and pre-shared key on both sides
questions.correct_rationale: Phase 1 failures come from IKE parameter or authentication mismatches.
questions.distractor_summary: Route propagation and Transit Gateway associations matter after the tunnel is up, and IKE does not use port 443.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Maintain routing and connectivity on AWS and hybrid networks
questions.question: A company adds a second Direct Connect connection for resiliency, but traffic still uses only one link. It wants both links to carry traffic. What should be configured?
options: Advertise a default route only over the second link
Set a longer AS path on both links
Advertise the same prefixes with equal attributes over both virtual interfaces so BGP can use equal-cost multipath
Disable BFD on the first link
questions.correct_rationale: When both paths have equal BGP attributes, traffic can be balanced across them.
questions.distractor_summary: A default route on one link creates a preference, equal prepending does not create balance by itself, and disabling BFD only slows failover.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Maintain routing and connectivity on AWS and hybrid networks
questions.question: Which tool can show the actual path and the blocking component when an EC2 instance cannot reach a database in another VPC?
options: AWS Cost Explorer
AWS Trusted Advisor cost checks
VPC Reachability Analyzer
Amazon Macie
questions.correct_rationale: Reachability Analyzer traces the configured path hop by hop and names the blocking component.
questions.distractor_summary: Cost tools and Macie do not analyze network paths.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Maintain routing and connectivity on AWS and hybrid networks
questions.question: Clients report intermittent failures connecting to an internet-facing NLB. Targets show as unhealthy only in one Availability Zone. What should be checked first?
options: The Route 53 DNSSEC configuration
The security groups, network ACLs, and health check settings for targets in that Availability Zone
The VPC's IPAM pool
The CloudFront cache policy
questions.correct_rationale: Zone-specific health failures usually point to configuration differences or problems in that zone.
questions.distractor_summary: DNSSEC, IPAM, and CloudFront caching do not cause zone-specific target health failures.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Monitor and analyze network traffic to troubleshoot and optimize connectivity patterns
questions.question: A security team needs full packet payloads from specific EC2 instances for analysis with an intrusion detection tool. What should be used?
options: VPC Traffic Mirroring to a target such as an NLB or Gateway Load Balancer in front of the analysis tools
VPC Flow Logs
CloudTrail data events
Route 53 query logs
questions.correct_rationale: Traffic Mirroring copies packets from network interfaces, including payloads, to monitoring targets.
questions.distractor_summary: Flow Logs record metadata only, CloudTrail records API calls, and query logs record DNS lookups.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Monitor and analyze network traffic to troubleshoot and optimize connectivity patterns
questions.question: Flow Logs show traffic accepted by a security group but rejected by a network ACL on the return path. What is the most likely cause?
options: Security groups are stateless
The route table lacks a local route
The flow log is in the wrong format
The network ACL does not allow the ephemeral port range for return traffic
questions.correct_rationale: Network ACLs are stateless, so return traffic on ephemeral ports needs an explicit allow rule.
questions.distractor_summary: Security groups are stateful, local routes always exist, and the log format does not cause rejections.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Monitor and analyze network traffic to troubleshoot and optimize connectivity patterns
questions.question: Which VPC Flow Logs field indicates whether traffic was allowed or denied?
options: log-status
tcp-flags
pkt-srcaddr
action
questions.correct_rationale: The action field records ACCEPT or REJECT for the traffic.
questions.distractor_summary: log-status reports the logging status, tcp-flags shows TCP flags, and pkt-srcaddr shows the original source address.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Monitor and analyze network traffic to troubleshoot and optimize connectivity patterns
questions.question: A team wants alerts when Direct Connect connection state changes or BGP goes down. What should they configure?
options: AWS Config conformance packs
Amazon Inspector findings
CloudWatch alarms on Direct Connect metrics such as ConnectionState and VirtualInterfaceBgpStatus, with notifications
S3 server access logs
questions.correct_rationale: Direct Connect publishes connection and virtual interface metrics to CloudWatch, which can trigger alarms.
questions.distractor_summary: Config, Inspector, and S3 access logs do not watch link state.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Monitor and analyze network traffic to troubleshoot and optimize connectivity patterns
questions.question: Users report slow performance to an application across Regions. The team wants to compare latency between AWS Regions and Availability Zones over time. What should be used?
options: VPC Flow Logs with the default format
AWS Network Manager Infrastructure Performance
AWS Health Dashboard only
AWS Cost and Usage Report
questions.correct_rationale: Infrastructure Performance shows latency between Regions and Availability Zones to help separate AWS network issues from application issues.
questions.distractor_summary: Default Flow Logs lack latency, the Health Dashboard shows events, and the cost report shows spending.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Monitor and analyze network traffic to troubleshoot and optimize connectivity patterns
questions.question: What does Amazon CloudWatch Internet Monitor measure?
options: Internet performance and availability between an application's users and AWS, by location and network provider
CPU usage of EC2 instances
DNS query counts inside a VPC
Packet payloads on a Transit Gateway
questions.correct_rationale: Internet Monitor uses AWS connectivity data to show internet health for an application's users.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not measure CPU, internal DNS queries, or packet payloads.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Monitor and analyze network traffic to troubleshoot and optimize connectivity patterns
questions.question: Flow Logs must be queried to find the top talkers in a VPC each day. What is a cost-efficient approach?
options: Publish Flow Logs to S3 in Parquet with hourly partitions, and query them with Amazon Athena
Load Flow Logs into an RDS database every hour
Download the logs and inspect them manually
Send Flow Logs to SQS
questions.correct_rationale: Parquet with partitions reduces data scanned by Athena, which keeps queries fast and cheap.
questions.distractor_summary: RDS loading adds cost and operations, manual review does not scale, and SQS is not a log store.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Monitor and analyze network traffic to troubleshoot and optimize connectivity patterns
questions.question: Instances in a private subnet cannot reach the internet through a NAT gateway. Flow Logs show the traffic leaving the instance. What should be checked next?
options: The instance's IAM role
The VPC's DHCP option set domain name
Route 53 private hosted zone associations
The private subnet route to the NAT gateway, the NAT gateway's subnet route to an internet gateway, and network ACLs on both subnets
questions.correct_rationale: NAT requires the right routes on both subnets and network ACLs that allow outbound and return traffic.
questions.distractor_summary: IAM roles, DHCP domain names, and private zones do not affect packet forwarding to the internet.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Monitor and analyze network traffic to troubleshoot and optimize connectivity patterns
questions.question: Which Transit Gateway CloudWatch metric helps detect traffic dropped because there was no route?
options: BytesIn
CPUUtilization
PacketDropCountNoRoute
HealthyHostCount
questions.correct_rationale: PacketDropCountNoRoute counts packets dropped because no matching route existed.
questions.distractor_summary: BytesIn measures volume, CPU utilization is for instances, and healthy host counts are for load balancers.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Monitor and analyze network traffic to troubleshoot and optimize connectivity patterns
questions.question: An application team wants to see which flows use the most bandwidth through a Transit Gateway across many accounts. What should be enabled?
options: Route 53 Resolver query logs
Transit Gateway Flow Logs sent to a central S3 bucket and analyzed with Athena
AWS CloudTrail management events
Amazon GuardDuty only
questions.correct_rationale: Transit Gateway Flow Logs record flow metadata for traffic crossing the Transit Gateway.
questions.distractor_summary: Query logs record DNS, CloudTrail records API calls, and GuardDuty detects threats rather than reporting bandwidth.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Optimize AWS networks for performance, reliability, and cost-effectiveness
questions.question: Two EC2 instances need the lowest possible latency and highest throughput between them for a tightly coupled workload. What should be used?
options: A spread placement group across Regions
A cluster placement group in one Availability Zone, with enhanced networking
Instances in different VPCs connected by VPN
A partition placement group across Availability Zones
questions.correct_rationale: Cluster placement groups place instances close together for low latency and high throughput.
questions.distractor_summary: Spread and partition groups favor isolation, and VPN between VPCs adds latency.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Optimize AWS networks for performance, reliability, and cost-effectiveness
questions.question: Data transfer costs are high because instances in private subnets download large files from S3 through NAT gateways. What change reduces cost?
options: Add an S3 gateway VPC endpoint and route S3 traffic through it
Add more NAT gateways
Move the instances into public subnets with public IPs
Use an interface endpoint for DynamoDB
questions.correct_rationale: Gateway endpoints for S3 carry no hourly or data processing charge and bypass the NAT gateway.
questions.distractor_summary: More NAT gateways add cost, public instances change the security posture, and a DynamoDB endpoint does not help S3 traffic.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Optimize AWS networks for performance, reliability, and cost-effectiveness
questions.question: What does enhanced networking with the Elastic Network Adapter provide?
options: Encryption of all traffic by default on every instance type
Automatic multi-Region routing
Free data transfer between Regions
Higher bandwidth, higher packet rates, and lower latency for supported instances
questions.correct_rationale: ENA uses SR-IOV to improve network performance on supported instance types.
questions.distractor_summary: ENA does not by itself encrypt all traffic, route between Regions, or remove transfer charges.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Optimize AWS networks for performance, reliability, and cost-effectiveness
questions.question: A company runs NAT gateways in one Availability Zone for a multi-AZ workload. What is the risk, and how should it be fixed?
options: There is no risk, because NAT gateways span Availability Zones
The NAT gateway will run out of IP addresses, so add more subnets
An outage in that zone breaks outbound access for all zones and adds cross-zone charges, so deploy a NAT gateway in each Availability Zone
The NAT gateway blocks inbound traffic, so remove it
questions.correct_rationale: NAT gateways are zonal, so one per Availability Zone avoids a single point of failure and cross-zone traffic.
questions.distractor_summary: NAT gateways do not span zones, IP exhaustion is not the main risk, and blocking unsolicited inbound traffic is intended behavior.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Optimize AWS networks for performance, reliability, and cost-effectiveness
questions.question: A company pays for a large amount of inter-AZ traffic between microservices behind internal ALBs. What change can reduce this cost while keeping availability?
options: Move all services to one Availability Zone
Replace the ALBs with public NLBs
Keep calls within the same Availability Zone where possible, for example by turning off cross-zone load balancing on the target group and keeping healthy targets in every zone
Use VPC peering between the services
questions.correct_rationale: Zonal affinity reduces cross-AZ data charges while healthy targets in each zone keep availability.
questions.distractor_summary: One zone reduces availability, public NLBs expose services, and peering does not reduce inter-AZ charges in one VPC.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Optimize AWS networks for performance, reliability, and cost-effectiveness
questions.question: Which AWS service provides private connectivity to many AWS services without traffic leaving the AWS network, through elastic network interfaces in a subnet?
options: Internet gateways
Interface VPC endpoints powered by AWS PrivateLink
Egress-only internet gateways
Carrier gateways
questions.correct_rationale: Interface endpoints give private IP access to supported services within the VPC.
questions.distractor_summary: Internet gateways and egress-only gateways route to the internet, and carrier gateways serve Wavelength Zones.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Optimize AWS networks for performance, reliability, and cost-effectiveness
questions.question: A Direct Connect hosted connection of 500 Mbps is saturated during nightly backups. What is the most direct fix?
options: Order a higher-capacity connection, or add another connection and balance traffic across them
Lower the MTU to 1300
Move the backups to a Site-to-Site VPN over the same circuit
Switch to a public virtual interface on the same connection
questions.correct_rationale: More capacity or more connections raise available bandwidth.
questions.distractor_summary: Lower MTU reduces efficiency, VPN over the same circuit does not add bandwidth, and changing VIF type does not add capacity.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Optimize AWS networks for performance, reliability, and cost-effectiveness
questions.question: Global users connect over TCP to an application in one Region and suffer high latency on long internet paths. The company cannot add Regions. What improves performance?
options: A larger instance type for the application
An additional NAT gateway
A Route 53 simple routing policy
AWS Global Accelerator, which brings traffic onto the AWS backbone at the nearest edge location
questions.correct_rationale: Global Accelerator reduces internet hops and uses the AWS network to the Region, which improves latency and consistency.
questions.distractor_summary: Larger instances do not shorten network paths, NAT gateways are for outbound traffic, and simple routing does not optimize paths.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Optimize AWS networks for performance, reliability, and cost-effectiveness
questions.question: What is a cost advantage of an S3 gateway endpoint compared with an S3 interface endpoint?
options: Gateway endpoints support on-premises access through Direct Connect
Gateway endpoints provide private IP addresses in subnets
Gateway endpoints work across Regions
Gateway endpoints have no hourly or per-GB charge
questions.correct_rationale: Gateway endpoints are free, while interface endpoints are billed per hour and per GB.
questions.distractor_summary: On-premises access, private IPs, and cross-Region use are features of interface endpoints or not supported at all.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Optimize AWS networks for performance, reliability, and cost-effectiveness
questions.question: A workload needs IPv6 internet access for outbound connections only, from private subnets. What should be used?
options: A NAT gateway for IPv6 only
A virtual private gateway
An egress-only internet gateway with routes for ::/0
A public IPv4 address on every instance
questions.correct_rationale: Egress-only internet gateways allow outbound IPv6 connections and block unsolicited inbound connections.
questions.distractor_summary: NAT gateways do not serve IPv6 this way, virtual private gateways connect VPNs, and IPv4 addresses do not apply to IPv6.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Implement and maintain network features to meet security and compliance needs and requirements
questions.question: A company needs stateful inspection, domain filtering, and intrusion prevention for traffic leaving its VPCs. Which managed service fits?
options: Security groups only
AWS Network Firewall
Network ACLs only
AWS Shield Standard
questions.correct_rationale: Network Firewall supports stateful rules, domain lists, and Suricata-compatible intrusion prevention rules.
questions.distractor_summary: Security groups and network ACLs do not filter domains or prevent intrusions, and Shield Standard protects against DDoS.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Implement and maintain network features to meet security and compliance needs and requirements
questions.question: Traffic between VPCs and to the internet must be inspected by third-party firewall appliances that scale horizontally. What design fits?
options: A Gateway Load Balancer in an inspection VPC, with Gateway Load Balancer endpoints in the routing path
An Application Load Balancer in front of the appliances
A NAT gateway in each spoke VPC
VPC peering to the appliance VPC
questions.correct_rationale: Gateway Load Balancer distributes traffic to appliances transparently and keeps flows sticky.
questions.distractor_summary: ALBs work at layer 7 and do not pass traffic transparently, NAT gateways do not inspect, and peering does not insert appliances in the path.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Implement and maintain network features to meet security and compliance needs and requirements
questions.question: Which statement about security groups is correct?
options: Security groups are stateful and support allow rules only
Security groups are stateless and support deny rules
Security groups apply to whole subnets
Security groups evaluate rules in number order
questions.correct_rationale: Security groups track connections and only allow traffic, while network ACLs are stateless and ordered.
questions.distractor_summary: The other statements describe network ACLs or are incorrect.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Implement and maintain network features to meet security and compliance needs and requirements
questions.question: A network ACL must block a single malicious IP address from reaching a subnet while allowing all other traffic. What should be done?
options: Add a deny rule in the security group
Add a deny rule with a higher number than the allow rules
Remove the subnet's route to the internet gateway
Add a deny rule for that IP address with a lower rule number than the allow rules
questions.correct_rationale: Network ACLs evaluate rules in order, so the deny must come before the broader allow.
questions.distractor_summary: Security groups have no deny rules, a later deny is never reached, and removing the route blocks everyone.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Implement and maintain network features to meet security and compliance needs and requirements
questions.question: A company must protect a public web application from large DDoS attacks and wants cost protection and access to the AWS response team. What should be used?
options: AWS Shield Standard alone
Security groups with rate limits
AWS Shield Advanced on the CloudFront distribution, load balancer, or Global Accelerator, along with AWS WAF
Network ACLs with a deny for all traffic
questions.correct_rationale: Shield Advanced adds enhanced detection, cost protection, and access to the Shield Response Team.
questions.distractor_summary: Shield Standard lacks those extras, security groups have no rate limits, and denying all traffic takes the application offline.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Implement and maintain network features to meet security and compliance needs and requirements
questions.question: Which AWS WAF rule type limits the number of requests from a single IP address over a time window?
options: A geographic match rule
A rate-based rule
An IP set rule that allows all
A size constraint rule
questions.correct_rationale: Rate-based rules block or count requests when one source exceeds a threshold.
questions.distractor_summary: Geographic, IP set, and size rules match other attributes.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Implement and maintain network features to meet security and compliance needs and requirements
questions.question: Security policy requires that S3 access from a VPC endpoint be limited to company buckets only. What should be configured?
options: A network ACL that blocks port 443
A VPC endpoint policy that allows access only to the company's bucket ARNs
A NAT gateway with a deny list
A security group on the gateway endpoint
questions.correct_rationale: Endpoint policies restrict which resources can be accessed through the endpoint.
questions.distractor_summary: Blocking port 443 breaks S3, NAT gateways do not filter by bucket, and gateway endpoints do not use security groups.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Implement and maintain network features to meet security and compliance needs and requirements
questions.question: Firewall rules must be applied consistently to Network Firewall deployments in every account in an organization. What should be used?
options: AWS Firewall Manager policies for Network Firewall
Manual rule updates in each account
AWS Config only
Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall only
questions.correct_rationale: Firewall Manager centrally deploys and manages firewall policies across accounts.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual changes drift, Config detects but does not deploy firewalls, and DNS Firewall filters DNS queries only.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Implement and maintain network features to meet security and compliance needs and requirements
questions.question: Which feature lets security groups be referenced in rules across VPCs attached to the same Transit Gateway?
options: Network ACL sharing
Gateway endpoint policies
Route 53 Resolver rules
Security group referencing support on the Transit Gateway
questions.correct_rationale: Transit Gateway security group referencing lets rules reference security groups in other attached VPCs in the same Region.
questions.distractor_summary: Network ACLs are not shared, endpoint policies control service access, and Resolver rules handle DNS.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Implement and maintain network features to meet security and compliance needs and requirements
questions.question: A company wants employees to access private applications without a VPN client, with access based on identity and device posture. Which service fits?
options: AWS Client VPN
A public ALB with IP allowlists
AWS Verified Access
An internet gateway with security groups
questions.correct_rationale: Verified Access evaluates identity and device signals for each request to private applications.
questions.distractor_summary: Client VPN needs a client, and public ALBs or internet gateways do not apply identity-based policies on their own.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Implement and maintain network features to meet security and compliance needs and requirements
questions.question: Outbound internet traffic must be restricted to an approved list of domains for workloads in private subnets. What is the best approach?
options: Use security groups with domain names in rules
Use network ACLs with domain names
Use AWS Network Firewall stateful domain list rules in the egress path
Use Route 53 public hosted zones
questions.correct_rationale: Network Firewall can inspect TLS SNI and HTTP host headers to allow only approved domains.
questions.distractor_summary: Security groups and network ACLs work with IP addresses, and hosted zones do not filter traffic.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Implement and maintain network features to meet security and compliance needs and requirements
questions.question: What does AWS Shield Standard provide?
options: A dedicated response team
Automatic protection against common network and transport layer DDoS attacks at no extra cost
Cost protection for scaling during attacks
Application layer rule management
questions.correct_rationale: Shield Standard is included and protects against common infrastructure DDoS attacks.
questions.distractor_summary: Response team, cost protection, and advanced application protections come with Shield Advanced and WAF.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Validate and audit security by using network monitoring and logging services
questions.question: A security team wants alerts on suspicious network activity such as port scanning and communication with known malicious IPs. Which service fits?
options: Amazon GuardDuty
AWS Cost Explorer
AWS Backup
AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager
questions.correct_rationale: GuardDuty analyzes Flow Logs, DNS logs, and CloudTrail events to detect threats.
questions.distractor_summary: The other choices manage cost, backups, and patching.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Validate and audit security by using network monitoring and logging services
questions.question: Auditors need a report of every path from the internet to EC2 instances that are open on any port. Which tool fits?
options: AWS Trusted Advisor cost checks
CloudWatch Logs Insights on application logs
AWS X-Ray
Network Access Analyzer with a scope for internet-reachable paths
questions.correct_rationale: Network Access Analyzer finds paths that match a defined scope, such as internet access to instances.
questions.distractor_summary: Cost checks, application logs, and tracing do not analyze network reachability.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Validate and audit security by using network monitoring and logging services
questions.question: Which service records API calls that change security groups, route tables, and network ACLs?
options: VPC Flow Logs
Route 53 query logs
Amazon CloudWatch Internet Monitor
AWS CloudTrail
questions.correct_rationale: CloudTrail logs API calls, including who made a change and when.
questions.distractor_summary: Flow Logs record traffic, query logs record DNS, and Internet Monitor measures internet health.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Validate and audit security by using network monitoring and logging services
questions.question: A company wants to detect security groups that allow unrestricted SSH and flag them automatically. What should be used?
options: VPC Flow Logs only
AWS Budgets
AWS Config managed rule for restricted SSH, with remediation
Amazon S3 Inventory
questions.correct_rationale: Config rules evaluate resource configurations and can trigger automatic remediation.
questions.distractor_summary: Flow Logs show traffic, not rule configuration, and Budgets and S3 Inventory are unrelated.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Validate and audit security by using network monitoring and logging services
questions.question: Network Firewall logs must be kept for one year and searched during investigations. What logging design fits?
options: Keep logs only in the firewall memory
Send alert and flow logs to S3 with lifecycle rules, and query them with Athena when needed
Send logs to SQS for long-term storage
Disable flow logs and keep only alerts
questions.correct_rationale: S3 gives durable, low-cost retention, and Athena can search the logs on demand.
questions.distractor_summary: Firewalls do not keep logs in memory for a year, SQS is not a log store, and dropping flow logs loses evidence.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Validate and audit security by using network monitoring and logging services
questions.question: Which AWS Security Hub feature helps track network security posture across accounts?
options: Aggregated findings and automated security checks against standards such as AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Packet capture
DNS resolution
Load balancing
questions.correct_rationale: Security Hub collects findings and runs checks, including network-related controls, across accounts.
questions.distractor_summary: Packet capture, DNS, and load balancing are other services' functions.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Validate and audit security by using network monitoring and logging services
questions.question: Investigators want to confirm whether a specific IP connected to an instance last week. Flow Logs are enabled. What should they do?
options: Query the Flow Logs for records with that IP as source or destination and the instance's interface
Check Route 53 health checks
Review the instance's CPU metrics
Check AWS Budgets reports
questions.correct_rationale: Flow Logs record source and destination IPs, ports, and actions for each interface.
questions.distractor_summary: Health checks, CPU metrics, and budgets do not record connections.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Validate and audit security by using network monitoring and logging services
questions.question: A team must prove that all VPCs in the organization have Flow Logs enabled, and fix any that do not. What should be implemented?
options: A monthly manual console check
An S3 bucket policy
A CloudFront function
An AWS Config organization rule that checks for VPC Flow Logs, with automatic remediation
questions.correct_rationale: Organization Config rules evaluate every account and can remediate missing Flow Logs.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual checks miss changes, and bucket policies and CloudFront functions do not enable logging.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Validate and audit security by using network monitoring and logging services
questions.question: Which AWS WAF feature records details of each inspected web request for analysis?
options: Shield Standard reports
VPC Flow Logs
WAF logging to CloudWatch Logs, S3, or Kinesis Data Firehose
Route 53 query logs
questions.correct_rationale: WAF logging captures request details and the rule that matched.
questions.distractor_summary: Shield reports, Flow Logs, and query logs do not record full web request details.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Validate and audit security by using network monitoring and logging services
questions.question: Security wants a dashboard of WAF blocked requests by rule and country. What is the simplest option?
options: Use EC2 instance metadata
Use the AWS WAF console metrics and CloudWatch, or query WAF logs with Athena and visualize the results
Use Direct Connect metrics
Use the AWS Pricing Calculator
questions.correct_rationale: WAF publishes metrics and logs that can be charted by rule and country.
questions.distractor_summary: Instance metadata, Direct Connect metrics, and pricing tools are unrelated.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Validate and audit security by using network monitoring and logging services
questions.question: GuardDuty reports DNS queries from an instance to a known command-and-control domain. What should be done to block these lookups across the organization?
options: Delete the GuardDuty finding
Add the domain to a Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall block list deployed through Firewall Manager, and investigate the instance
Disable DNS in all VPCs
Increase the instance size
questions.correct_rationale: DNS Firewall blocks lookups centrally, while the instance should be isolated and investigated.
questions.distractor_summary: Deleting findings hides the issue, disabling DNS breaks everything, and instance size is irrelevant.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Validate and audit security by using network monitoring and logging services
questions.question: Which service gives an interactive visualization of related security findings and network activity to support investigations?
options: Amazon Detective
AWS Firewall Manager
AWS Certificate Manager
AWS DataSync
questions.correct_rationale: Detective builds behavior graphs from logs to help investigate findings.
questions.distractor_summary: Firewall Manager manages rules, ACM manages certificates, and DataSync moves data.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Implement and maintain confidentiality of data and communications of the network
questions.question: All traffic between clients and an ALB must be encrypted, and certificates must renew automatically. What should be used?
options: An HTTP listener with a security group
A self-signed certificate on each target, renewed manually
A Network ACL that blocks port 80
An HTTPS listener with a certificate from AWS Certificate Manager
questions.correct_rationale: ACM provides managed public certificates with automatic renewal for ALB HTTPS listeners.
questions.distractor_summary: HTTP is unencrypted, manual certificates risk expiry, and blocking port 80 does not encrypt traffic.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Implement and maintain confidentiality of data and communications of the network
questions.question: Traffic between an ALB and its targets must also be encrypted. What should be configured?
options: HTTP target groups with a private subnet
A network ACL on the target subnet
HTTPS target groups with certificates on the targets
An S3 gateway endpoint
questions.correct_rationale: HTTPS target groups make the ALB use TLS to the targets for end-to-end encryption.
questions.distractor_summary: Private subnets and network ACLs do not encrypt, and gateway endpoints are unrelated.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Implement and maintain confidentiality of data and communications of the network
questions.question: Which AWS service issues private certificates for internal services and mutual TLS?
options: AWS Key Management Service only
AWS WAF
AWS Private Certificate Authority
AWS Shield
questions.correct_rationale: AWS Private CA issues private certificates for internal endpoints and client authentication.
questions.distractor_summary: KMS manages keys, WAF filters requests, and Shield protects against DDoS.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Implement and maintain confidentiality of data and communications of the network
questions.question: Data in transit between two VPCs in different Regions must be encrypted. The VPCs are connected by inter-Region peering. Is extra configuration needed?
options: Yes, peering traffic is sent in clear text over the internet
No, inter-Region peering traffic is encrypted on the AWS backbone, although applications can still add TLS
Yes, an IPsec VPN must be added on top of the peering
No, because peering traffic never leaves the source Region
questions.correct_rationale: AWS encrypts inter-Region peering traffic, and it stays on the AWS global network.
questions.distractor_summary: Peering traffic does not cross the public internet, a VPN is not required, and inter-Region traffic does leave the Region.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Implement and maintain confidentiality of data and communications of the network
questions.question: A company requires that only specific clients holding a certificate can connect to an internal API behind an ALB. What should be configured?
options: Mutual TLS on the ALB listener with a trust store of approved CA certificates
An HTTP listener with an IP allowlist only
A Gateway Load Balancer in front of the ALB
A larger instance type
questions.correct_rationale: ALB mutual TLS verifies client certificates against a trust store.
questions.distractor_summary: IP allowlists do not check certificates, Gateway Load Balancers serve appliances, and instance size is irrelevant.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Implement and maintain confidentiality of data and communications of the network
questions.question: Which Direct Connect feature encrypts traffic at layer 2 on supported dedicated connections?
options: BFD
Link aggregation group
Jumbo frames
MACsec
questions.correct_rationale: MACsec provides layer 2 encryption on supported dedicated connections.
questions.distractor_summary: BFD detects failures, LAGs bundle links, and jumbo frames change frame size.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Implement and maintain confidentiality of data and communications of the network
questions.question: Users connect from laptops to private resources in a VPC and need encrypted connections managed by AWS. What fits best?
options: A public IP on each resource
A Site-to-Site VPN from each laptop
VPC peering to each laptop
AWS Client VPN with authentication through Active Directory, SAML, or certificates
questions.correct_rationale: Client VPN provides managed OpenVPN-based remote access with authentication options.
questions.distractor_summary: Public IPs expose resources, Site-to-Site VPN is for networks, and peering connects VPCs.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Implement and maintain confidentiality of data and communications of the network
questions.question: A company wants to keep API calls to AWS services from leaving its private network and to restrict which principals use the endpoint. What should be configured?
options: Public service endpoints over the internet
A NAT gateway with a deny list
Interface VPC endpoints with endpoint policies, reached from on premises over Direct Connect or VPN
CloudFront in front of the AWS APIs
questions.correct_rationale: Interface endpoints keep service traffic private, and endpoint policies restrict which principals and actions are allowed.
questions.distractor_summary: Public endpoints cross the internet, NAT gateways do not restrict principals, and CloudFront is not used for AWS service APIs.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Implement and maintain confidentiality of data and communications of the network
questions.question: Which TLS policy setting on a load balancer listener controls which protocol versions and ciphers are allowed?
options: The target group stickiness setting
The security policy
The health check path
The deregistration delay
questions.correct_rationale: Security policies define allowed TLS versions and cipher suites.
questions.distractor_summary: Stickiness, health checks, and deregistration delay do not control TLS.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Implement and maintain confidentiality of data and communications of the network
questions.question: Sensitive S3 data must be reachable only from a specific VPC endpoint. What should be added?
options: A bucket policy that denies access unless the request comes through that VPC endpoint
A network ACL that blocks S3 prefix lists
A security group on the bucket
An internet gateway route for S3
questions.correct_rationale: Bucket policies can use the aws:SourceVpce condition to require access through a specific endpoint.
questions.distractor_summary: Blocking prefix lists breaks access, buckets do not have security groups, and internet routing defeats the goal.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Implement and maintain confidentiality of data and communications of the network
questions.question: A VPN between on premises and AWS must use stronger cryptography than the defaults. What can be changed?
options: The tunnel options for IKE version, encryption and integrity algorithms, and Diffie-Hellman groups
The VPC CIDR range
The BGP ASN
The subnet route tables
questions.correct_rationale: Site-to-Site VPN tunnel options let administrators restrict the allowed cryptographic settings.
questions.distractor_summary: CIDR ranges, ASNs, and route tables do not change encryption.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Implement and maintain confidentiality of data and communications of the network
questions.question: Which service manages encryption keys used for data stored by AWS network logging destinations such as S3 buckets?
options: AWS Shield
AWS Global Accelerator
AWS Transit Gateway
AWS Key Management Service
questions.correct_rationale: KMS creates and controls keys used for server-side encryption of stored logs.
questions.distractor_summary: Shield, Global Accelerator, and Transit Gateway do not manage keys.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Implement and maintain confidentiality of data and communications of the network
questions.question: A team wants network logs encrypted with a customer managed key and wants to control who can decrypt them. What should be done?
options: Use public buckets with object ACLs
Store logs on EC2 instance store volumes
Configure S3 default encryption with a KMS customer managed key and restrict the key policy
Disable encryption to simplify access
questions.correct_rationale: A customer managed KMS key with a restricted key policy controls who can read the logs.
questions.distractor_summary: Public buckets, instance store, and disabled encryption fail the requirement.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Implement and maintain confidentiality of data and communications of the network
questions.question: Containers in Amazon ECS must communicate with each other over encrypted connections without changing application code. What should be considered?
options: Security groups with larger CIDR blocks
A service mesh such as Amazon ECS Service Connect with TLS enabled
Network ACLs in the task subnet
Placing all tasks in one Availability Zone
questions.correct_rationale: ECS Service Connect can encrypt traffic between services by using certificates from AWS Private CA.
questions.distractor_summary: Security groups and network ACLs do not encrypt, and placement does not provide encryption.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Maintain routing and connectivity on AWS and hybrid networks
questions.question: A VPC is running out of IP addresses in its primary CIDR block. Workloads must keep running. What should the network team do?
options: Change the primary CIDR block in place
Add a secondary IPv4 CIDR block to the VPC and create new subnets from it
Delete the VPC and recreate it with a larger range
Assign public IPs to all new instances
questions.correct_rationale: VPCs support secondary CIDR blocks, which add address space without disrupting existing subnets.
questions.distractor_summary: The primary block cannot be changed in place, recreation causes an outage, and public IPs do not fix private address shortage.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Maintain routing and connectivity on AWS and hybrid networks
questions.question: After a Direct Connect maintenance event, traffic did not fail back to the primary link when it returned. BGP shows both paths with the same preference. What should be done?
options: Set deterministic preferences, such as local preference on premises and AS path prepending on the backup, so the primary is always preferred when up
Leave the configuration as is and wait
Delete the backup virtual interface
Change the VPC CIDR range
questions.correct_rationale: Explicit BGP preferences make the primary path win whenever it is available.
questions.distractor_summary: Waiting does not change path selection, deleting the backup removes resilience, and CIDR changes are unrelated.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Maintain routing and connectivity on AWS and hybrid networks
questions.question: Which Transit Gateway feature lets you add a static route that covers several prefixes as one entry for attachments that need it?
options: A blackhole route
Appliance mode
Multicast domain
A prefix list reference in the Transit Gateway route table
questions.correct_rationale: Managed prefix lists can be referenced in Transit Gateway route tables to manage groups of CIDR blocks.
questions.distractor_summary: Blackhole routes drop traffic, appliance mode keeps flows symmetric, and multicast domains deliver multicast.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Maintain routing and connectivity on AWS and hybrid networks
questions.question: Engineers want to know when routes in a Transit Gateway route table change unexpectedly. What should they use?
options: Amazon S3 event notifications
AWS Budgets alerts
AWS Network Manager route analysis and events sent to EventBridge, with notifications
AWS Backup reports
questions.correct_rationale: Network Manager records topology and route changes and can send events for alerting.
questions.distractor_summary: S3 events, Budgets, and Backup reports do not track routing changes.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Monitor and analyze network traffic to troubleshoot and optimize connectivity patterns
questions.question: An application intermittently drops connections through a NAT gateway under heavy load. Which CloudWatch metric should be checked?
options: HealthyHostCount
NumberOfObjects
ErrorPortAllocation, which shows when the NAT gateway could not allocate a source port
CPUCreditBalance
questions.correct_rationale: Port allocation errors show the NAT gateway ran out of ports for a destination, which can be fixed by adding IP addresses or spreading destinations.
questions.distractor_summary: The other metrics belong to load balancers, S3, and burstable instances.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Monitor and analyze network traffic to troubleshoot and optimize connectivity patterns
questions.question: A team suspects packet loss between an on-premises site and a VPC over a VPN. What is a good way to measure it continuously?
options: Read the VPC route table
Use CloudWatch Network Monitor probes from the VPC to on-premises destinations
Enable S3 access logging
Check IAM Access Analyzer
questions.correct_rationale: Network Monitor sends probes over hybrid paths and reports packet loss and latency.
questions.distractor_summary: Route tables show configuration, and S3 logging and IAM Access Analyzer do not measure loss.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Monitor and analyze network traffic to troubleshoot and optimize connectivity patterns
questions.question: Which Flow Logs setting reduces log volume by recording aggregated flows over a longer interval?
options: A maximum aggregation interval of 10 minutes rather than 1 minute
Choosing the ALL traffic type
Adding every custom field
Enabling Traffic Mirroring
questions.correct_rationale: A longer aggregation interval produces fewer records for the same traffic.
questions.distractor_summary: Logging all traffic and adding fields increase volume, and Traffic Mirroring copies packets.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Optimize AWS networks for performance, reliability, and cost-effectiveness
questions.question: A company wants to lower cost for many interface VPC endpoints duplicated in 50 VPCs. What design helps?
options: Add more interface endpoints in each VPC
Use public endpoints over NAT gateways for everything
Create a gateway endpoint for every service
Centralize the interface endpoints in a shared services VPC, reached through a Transit Gateway, with private hosted zones for the endpoint names
questions.correct_rationale: Centralized endpoints are shared by many VPCs, which reduces the number of hourly endpoint charges.
questions.distractor_summary: More endpoints add cost, NAT data charges can exceed savings, and gateway endpoints exist only for S3 and DynamoDB.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Optimize AWS networks for performance, reliability, and cost-effectiveness
questions.question: A latency-sensitive application in one Region must serve users in a metropolitan area with single-digit millisecond latency. What option fits best?
options: Add a NAT gateway in a different Region
Increase the VPC CIDR size
Use a larger Direct Connect connection to the Region
Deploy part of the workload to an AWS Local Zone near those users
questions.correct_rationale: Local Zones place compute and storage closer to users in specific metro areas.
questions.distractor_summary: NAT gateways and CIDR sizes do not reduce user latency, and Direct Connect serves corporate networks rather than end users.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Optimize AWS networks for performance, reliability, and cost-effectiveness
questions.question: What is a benefit of enabling Direct Connect SiteLink?
options: It encrypts traffic at layer 2
It provides a public IP to every VPC
It lets on-premises sites send traffic to each other over the AWS network through Direct Connect locations without passing through a Region
It removes the need for BGP
questions.correct_rationale: SiteLink connects on-premises sites through the AWS backbone using Direct Connect locations.
questions.distractor_summary: MACsec encrypts at layer 2, SiteLink does not assign public IPs, and BGP is still used.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Implement and maintain network features to meet security and compliance needs and requirements
questions.question: A company must make sure no VPC in the organization can attach an internet gateway except approved egress VPCs. What should be used?
options: Security groups in every account
A service control policy that denies creating or attaching internet gateways except for an approved role
A Route 53 private hosted zone
AWS Budgets alerts
questions.correct_rationale: SCPs set guardrails for API actions across accounts in AWS Organizations.
questions.distractor_summary: Security groups filter traffic, hosted zones resolve names, and Budgets track spend.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Implement and maintain network features to meet security and compliance needs and requirements
questions.question: Network Firewall must inspect traffic entering a VPC from the internet before it reaches public ALBs. What routing is needed?
options: An internet gateway route table (edge association) that sends traffic for the ALB subnets to the firewall endpoints, and ALB subnet routes back through the firewall
A security group on the internet gateway
A NAT gateway in front of the firewall
VPC peering between the firewall and ALB subnets
questions.correct_rationale: Ingress routing with an edge-associated route table steers inbound traffic through the firewall endpoints.
questions.distractor_summary: Internet gateways do not take security groups, NAT gateways handle outbound traffic, and peering does not apply within one VPC.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Implement and maintain network features to meet security and compliance needs and requirements
questions.question: Which AWS WAF feature uses AWS-maintained rule sets for common threats such as SQL injection?
options: AWS Managed Rules rule groups
Shield Advanced proactive engagement
Network ACL default rules
VPC endpoint policies
questions.correct_rationale: Managed rule groups provide preconfigured protections maintained by AWS.
questions.distractor_summary: Shield engagement, network ACLs, and endpoint policies do not provide web application rule sets.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Implement and maintain network features to meet security and compliance needs and requirements
questions.question: A third-party SaaS provider exposes its service through PrivateLink. The company wants to prevent its endpoint from being used for anything other than that service. What should be configured?
options: An internet gateway with a deny list
A public NLB in the company's VPC
A NAT gateway route to the provider
An interface endpoint with security groups that allow only the required clients and ports
questions.correct_rationale: Endpoint security groups restrict which clients can use the endpoint, and the endpoint reaches only that service.
questions.distractor_summary: Internet gateways, public NLBs, and NAT routes are not part of a private endpoint design.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Validate and audit security by using network monitoring and logging services
questions.question: A compliance team wants to compare current network configurations to a baseline and see history of changes to a security group. What should be used?
options: VPC Flow Logs
CloudWatch metrics
AWS Config resource configuration history and timeline
Route 53 health checks
questions.correct_rationale: Config records configuration changes over time for supported resources.
questions.distractor_summary: Flow Logs record traffic, metrics show performance, and health checks test endpoints.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Validate and audit security by using network monitoring and logging services
questions.question: Logs from VPC Flow Logs, Route 53 Resolver, and Network Firewall must be normalized into a common format for a security lake. Which service fits?
options: AWS DataSync
Amazon Security Lake, which uses the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework
Amazon Data Firehose without transformation
Amazon S3 Glacier only
questions.correct_rationale: Security Lake collects AWS log sources and normalizes them into OCSF in a central data lake.
questions.distractor_summary: DataSync moves files, Firehose alone does not normalize, and Glacier only archives.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Validate and audit security by using network monitoring and logging services
questions.question: What can Reachability Analyzer help prove during an audit?
options: That encryption keys are rotated
That a specific path between two resources is or is not reachable based on configuration
That instances are patched
That costs are within budget
questions.correct_rationale: Reachability Analyzer gives evidence about network paths by analyzing configuration.
questions.distractor_summary: Key rotation, patching, and costs are checked by other services.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Implement and maintain confidentiality of data and communications of the network
questions.question: A CloudFront distribution must use HTTPS between viewers and edge locations and also to the origin. What settings are needed?
options: Set the viewer protocol policy to redirect HTTP to HTTPS or HTTPS only, and set the origin protocol policy to HTTPS only
Set the viewer protocol policy to HTTP and HTTPS
Enable compression
Use a larger origin instance
questions.correct_rationale: Both the viewer and origin protocol policies must require HTTPS for end-to-end encryption.
questions.distractor_summary: Allowing HTTP leaves traffic unencrypted, and compression and instance size are unrelated.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Implement and maintain confidentiality of data and communications of the network
questions.question: An organization requires that TLS 1.0 and 1.1 not be used anywhere on public endpoints. What should be done for ALBs and CloudFront?
options: Turn off HTTPS listeners
Use self-signed certificates
Block port 443 with network ACLs
Select security policies that allow only TLS 1.2 or later on listeners and distributions
questions.correct_rationale: Modern security policies remove older TLS versions while keeping HTTPS available.
questions.distractor_summary: Turning off HTTPS or blocking 443 breaks secure access, and self-signed certificates do not control protocol versions.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Implement and maintain confidentiality of data and communications of the network
questions.question: Which statement about traffic within a VPC between supported Nitro instance types is correct?
options: All traffic in every VPC is sent in clear text across the internet
Encryption requires a VPN between subnets
Traffic between supported Nitro instances in the same or peered VPCs is automatically encrypted in transit
Encryption is only available with Direct Connect
questions.correct_rationale: AWS encrypts traffic between supported Nitro-based instances automatically, in addition to any application TLS.
questions.distractor_summary: VPC traffic does not cross the internet, and neither VPN nor Direct Connect is required for this encryption.
